As a longtime fan of the Talisman franchise, I will recommend the Digital Edition.  But not without qualification.  While an ably faithful translation of the boardgame experience, the AI is simply not challenging enough for veteran players of the game.  It's not that the AI will never win against a seasoned player.  It can.  But things have to go extremely right for the AI, and extremely wrong for the player, for this to happen.   Even with the wonky AI, I still find myself enjying the game.  And I believe most folks familiar with the game will, as well.
If you've never played Talisman, the AI is actually a benefit, as it keeps the game from being too punishing to neophyte players.  It's not that Talisman is an overly complex game.  But there is a lot of information to absorb.  The starter set alone boasts over a dozen playable characters, all of whom have multiple special abilities and differing alignments; there are five attributes for each character; there are nearly one hundred event cards, spells, etc.  So you get the idea.  There's a bit to learn and the AI allows games to extend the learning curve.
If reviews were given on a scoring basis as opposed to a simple recommend/not recommend, I would score Talisman: Digital Edition a solid 8.  In spite of the AI, the overall gameplay experience is fun for those who like board games or fantasy settings and there is a lot of replayability to be had.

This game is pretty good. It lives up to being the Stealth-Top-down-shooter-rogue-lite-dungeon-crawler-strange-but-awesome-hybrid-megagame. The gameplay is very fun. There are many ways to go about each level, whether it is to just rambro it and just go ham, stealth through a level without being seen, or do a weird combination of both. The controls are very simple, so if you are new to the game you won't get get confused by any combos or other stuff like that. The game also has a lot of game mechanics that are very easy to learn. They are all pretty much self explanatory. This game is also SO much fun with other people, especially friends. Being able to work to together or just to mess around together is so much fun.
One problem I do have with the game is that it is overpriced. I think $15 is a bit much for a game like this. Granted I did get it on sale for $7.50, but I think that is still overpriced. With the content inside it, its more of a 5 or 4 dollar game. This game is no where near a Hyper Light Drifter or a Transistor, so it shouldn't be almost worth as much as those games. Another problem I have with this game is that, even thought the gameplay is fun, a lot of the mission are quite linear. It is usually along the lines of "Retrieve this item" or "Neutralize this person". These missions show up a lot, and can get really boring.
All in all, this game is pretty good. I think if the game were to change so that it would have more missions to do  and maybe lower the price, this game would be great!

It also remind me of RPGs beacause of the class system, level ups and the overall progression of your character.

This game is a ton of fun (when you see the guy you need to kill walking in its own flame thrower for exemple) but still remains stressful (when you failed your backstab and see an army of bad guys shooting at you). And the balance between going berserk and being a ghost is well drawn: they both makes you feel strong at first, but when you ♥♥♥♥ up....well you'll understand.
If you love Rogue-likes, buy it and if you don't like them give it a try, it feels similar and different at the same time so it might suit you.

A superb return to a very popular classic with many improvements, not least of which are the excellent graphics.
A strong AI together with scalable difficulty levels provides as much challenge as you can handle and the tutorial battles should ease the new player into the game nicely.
With multiple ways to play including set-piece historical battles, multi-battle campaigns, random battles and campaigns, user-made battles  and campaigns, there is a huge amount of replayability.

Other reviews have offered summaries of what the game is about. I will note two things about it that stand out:
1) Variety of factions. From Indian armies, reliant on archers and war elephants, to the legions of Rome, the horsemen of the steppes, the warbands of the Gauls, and everything in between. All these armies have distinct fighting styles and must be managed very differently on the battlefield.
2) Narrative. Every battle you fight in this game creates stories: the elephants, panicked by javelins, crashing through the ranks of their own side, disordering their formations. The cavalry charge breaking through the flank and crashing into the enemy rear just in the nick of time. The triarii grimly advancing to the gap in the ranks of the principes.
Basically, if you're interested in the military history of the time period, get this game, it's a steal at $30. Plus, the developers are already working on the first DLC. If we're lucky, the completed game will someday include everything from the Persian Wars to the Renaissance.

Field of Glory II is simply the best turn based tactical game for the "ancient" period. If you want to play historical, satisfying battles set in "rise of rome" age, it's a golden heaven. almost 50 nations (ranging from Indians to Bactrians, some of them never seen in other PC games other than the first FOG) with lots of variation in the army lists - 6 Carthaginian lists, ie, made to deploy the exact army in different areas and years.
The graphics are really good: when you look at FOGII on your PC, it's like to see a tabletop wargame battle with 15mm soldiers. Light years from the first FOG graphics. Note: now you move on a square grid.

Field of Glory II instantly captured my imagination. 10/10, and I get the sense it's just going to improve.
The game consists of vast choices in battles -- campaign style, with brief historical contexts, choices, and forces continuing from one battle to the next.  There are also historical battles, plus a seemingly endless supply of armies to try out in custom battles.  It's really easy to set up and surprisingly intuitive.  If you play a custom battle and don't care about setup, the game automatically chooses two armies that might have faced each other in history.  It's a great feature.  Of course, you can set up the exact perameters you want as well -- there are plenty of choices.
It seems to be based on a tabletop game of the same name, so the maps are squarish and units have square areas of control.  That's not normally my thing, but it doesn't bother me here at all.  The graphics are good and the mechanics make sense.
Battles are seriously fun.  One satisfying mechanic occurs if you're able to really flank and break a wing of the enemy army.  Each time a unit routs, nearby units can lose organization or break as well.  If they're already teetering, a good maneuver can shatter an entire line in a turn.  There was one campaign, in a Pontus vs Rome battle, where my mediocre troops were desperately holding high ground against veteran legionaires.  My shock cavalry was able to chase off enemy support troops and smash into the Romans from the flanks, turning the battle in only a few turns.  There are so many 'stories' in each battle, and the game really lends itself to the imagination and getting caught up.
PROS:
- Gorgeous graphics, smooth gameplay and fast loadtimes
- Numerous campaigns already, plus polished user-released ones are already available via an in-game menu
- More factions than I can count, from Britain to India and literally everywhere in between
- More army/unit choices than I can count, with different periods from the 'Rise of Rome' represented.
- Satisfying, realistic mechanics.
- Intuitive controls
-  WAR ELEPHANTS
- Indo-Greeks
- Community content is already pouring in, and the devs make the best ones available for download in-game
CONS:
- Wish there was more of a map for the campaigns - the choices feel less impactful without seeing territory expand
- Campaigns sometimes tell you that your faction lost a battle, but you can't fight it.  Being able to fight a losing battle, but trying to limit losses and inflict damage to the enemy, can help immersion.
- More zoom please!  Ground level would be nice.

It's a pretty good stategy game that allows you to play battles and campaigns involving most of factions and nations of the ancient world before the emergence of the Roman Empire. It is a worthy successor to the Field of Glory and will provide a great base for future expansions. It's fun to play, easy to use, and custom battles allow great replayability. It's quite worth the price, although not perfect.
1. Graphics are great and 3D units are both detailed and rather accurate. At a glance you can see the unit's armor and weapons. Animation is really good and it's fun to see unit shiver when panicked or shouting a war cry when you are approaching. One issue I have is that Greek veteran hoplites are bearing Spartan insignia on the shield, which looks odd if you wish to play as Athens vs Sparta for example.
2. Finally a very good AI, which reminds of me of Pike & Shot. It doesn't make stupid mistakes and can proceed throughout the battle rather smoothly, unlike AGEOD or John Tiller ones. It's great to finally see a worthy opponent.
3. Campaigns are pretty good and can make you feel like a general of the time. Overall, it's pretty similar to how it's done in other, similar games, but fun nonetheless.
4. Nice random map generation, though by no means perfected yet - sometimes for example it creates a river almost in the middle of your troops, so some soldiers are on the other side, while there is a lot of empty space on the other side.
5. Rules are pretty simple yet quite realistic. The game is not as complicated as Gary Grigsby's behemoths and very easy to learn, yet hard to master if you wish to play on higher difficulty or a superior enemy. You can try very different things too, some more difficult than others - you can set the battle to have a stronger army and make them easy to learn the ropes, or tweak the settings to face the enemy that's has twice as many soldiers as you, or face the dreaded Romans as Gauls or Greeks and turn the tide. You can try really challenging real battles, especially so if you are playing as the side that has lost historically, and the game tells you which side is that, which is probably very good for the laymen.
6. PBEM is a very good choice for the multiplayer and works well despite being really old.
7. The game simulates battle between many different types of armies - you get armies that are melee based like the Romans or Greeks, as well as the Parthians or Armenians whose armies consist mostly of skirmishers. You can mix and match - see how hard is to fight as a phalanx against skirmishing army that keeps running away, or see how shooting armies fight each others like Armenians vs Parthians. Overall, you can really experience tactical and organizational differences which means a lot of fun through comparing different styles.
8. The routing systems keeps the game pretty realistic - forces don't fight till the end, after suffering hard losses they will simply escape, and too many routing units can make your entire line desert their positions and run for their lives. This is how battles were won back then and the game simulates it well.
1. The game is still not stable. When setting my units the game gets clunky, moves all over the place, and there are quite a few CTDs saying that I can't place troops somewhere and there's a certain exception and the game has to crash.
2. Aforementioned problems with random map generation which can make it hard for you to place your army by splitting it in half for example.
3. The game doesn't really simulate Roman organization beyond a simple cohort unless you use an editor or play existing battles - you get a certain amount of units and you deploy them - you don't deploy a whole legion or two for example, you develop like 6 cohorts, or 8 cohorts, and they don't fight as a group either, each cohort is independent. Also, there is no first cohort variant (made of double-strength centuries) which is a shame. Especially so in custom battles where you have a certain amount of units that you are allowed to choose from, which is not always accurate.
If you' re a history buff who likes some simple fun of a tabletop game, you will enjoy this one a lot. It's a bit buggy for me, but they will probably fix it soon, as the issues are rather minor. Overall, it is a really good game that will suit the grognards just as much as those who look for a simple, yet accurate game. You can make it simple or brutal with several different difficulty settings and the ability to customize your battles. I hope they will expand the series and we will be able to command some Imperial and Late Roman armies, or perhaps some Bronze Age ones. It certainly provides a very good foundation for expansions.

A new era for an ancient game.
This is probably the best game Slitherine released so far.
Originally based on the tabletopgame miniature game Field of Glory, but recreated in one of the most user friendliest engines Slitherine created so far for some classic games in the past. Pike & Shot, Battle Academy, Sengoku, Hell and more recently Warhammer Sanctus Reach.
The rough edges of the engine are history, the pixelated armies are fully animated 3D unit models now, the UI style perfectly fits the ancient theme and together with some finetuning and tweaks it's ultra friendly, even to them who never played a wargame before.
While in P&S, the majority of fights was shooting based, in FOG II, the majority of the battles are a melee bloodfest.
In a few turns the atmospheric, well designed, nicely colored and peaceful map, turns into a major bloodbath with hundreds of animated units fighting for their nation.
The terrain, the zones of control, the warbands and the positioning of your units are all crucial for turning the tides of battle. How detailed the information is returned to the player is fully customizable. You can set the Line of sight overlay, the detailed after battle reports, the detailed unit description and ZOC layers in the tools menu.
Tattered flags, shaking units, ambushes, skrimishes and units running away from the map are all add to immersion.
Those maps can be medium sized to widely open and there are many different kinds of terrain settings, like dessert wars with Eastern armies, and European agritectural fields. As a player you can choose between a tutorial campaign based on three unique scenarios. A detailed list of scenarios, a lot of campaigns to choose from, all with random elements so they never play the same twice, usermade scenarios already in the first week of release from returning FOG 1 players and a random battle generator as if it was not already enough.
This is an adult men toy box and if there is one game I want to see a DLC list for, bigger then that from CK II or EU IV, it's for FOG II.
The game have only favorite ratings from previous players from the series, even them who where skeptical about turning from hexes to squares at first. Don't forget that even a square have eight sides! Those critiques are now desiging  maps for FOG II ;-)
The game mechanism are highly complex. There is a beautiful designed manual with over 150 pages (included in both Slitherine and Steam release as .pdf, and sold sep as paperback on Slitherine store) that helps you overcome the complex mechanism about ZOC, LOS, POA's etc etc
But even without reading the manual the game is new player friendly enough to dive right in and start with the excellent tutorials or random generated battle. Learn while you play.
The ancient PBEM system which exists since the invention of E-MAIL, is actually the most modern and refreshing MP system nowadays. In times where people only have little time left to play games this system should be implemented in all TBS games. You play your turn when your want, eventually have many MP games open, you receive an e-mail or ingame message when it's your turn again. No need to make appointments with random strangers in different timezones, that's simply handled by the game.

This is probably the blandest platformer I have ever played. All levels fit on one screen, and objects are limited to blocks, spikes, springs, and occasionally a key. Gameplay does not vary at all between levels, and there aren't very many of them. The game also features a random level generator which spits out garbage that often is either impossible, or can be won by running to the right and jumping over one pit. The controls are bad, with it being difficult to guage the time you need to jump to bounce high off a spring, especially after they start sinking into the ground after you bounce on them a few times. The stats are completely broken, with the game awarding my the 50 deaths and 100 deaths achievements the first time I died, and the 1000 deaths achievement a few deaths, and less than a minute later. The game requires you to upload something to the workshop for one of the achievements, so expect the workshop to be flooded with garbage from people who just want the achievement.
I can't possibly recommend this unless you get it as part of a bundle, or it is less than $1, and you want easy achievements.

An intresting game with a fun fighting mechanic and satfisfying action.  Getting it for less the $10 was a steal for myself, and I believe I have gotten my moneys worth.
Cons
- Bugs
- Servers
- Weapon Balancing
- Solo Missions
- Enemy A.I
- Lack of Players
- Groggy Mechanic
- Skill upgrade
I've played this game for quite some time with a variety of skilled people.  Playing some of the best with their perfered weapons and new players who don't know what they are doing.  Almost all if not everyone I have met, has always had a problem with bugs and the server.  Constantly getting stuck in walls, on the elevator of a certain map, falling down a pit slightly to be caught on the very edge of the walls, and falling out of the map to only meet your doom.  The server has been a big concern as this game heavily relies on a players ability to grasp timing.  If one player is lagging slightly it's very noticeable.  If one player is lagging like crazy it's very noticeable.  You can slash away at them and someone how they jump away from you without harm.  Or it can be vice-versa where you're that player who is lagging like crazy.  You'll perform a grapple or simply block on your screen effortlessly, meanwhile the other player is beating the living♥♥♥♥♥♥out of you as for them, you're simply standing there.
Weapon balancing is a bit of an issue as many people complain that certain things are "Broken".  I've been bashed on and on about using a certain weapon as it is considered "broken" by the community.  Simply put:
- shield has a stun unlike any other.  Capable of performing an infinite loop combo that annoys the♥♥♥♥♥♥out of people as they can't break free from it.  As well as having the greatest block capability, which for obvious reasons it should since it's a shield, but many people complain that this is too op.
- Greatsword has a standard mouse click attack that once the first hit lands, you seem to not be able to break free from it's grasp and just die to the combo.
The solo missions are absolutely boring.  I only force myself to play it as no other players are on.  The first you play you enter a cutscene where your character runs out of a cooridor looking around and then you are able to use your character again.  I'm not too sure if it's because it's part of the story but I feel the cutscene was unnecessary.  You're told to hold off a horde of goblins that look a lot like giant wingless bats.  They look nothing like the typical so called goblin, but this is their game so they can make it look like whatever.  But, that leads me to the enemy a.i or lack there of.  It just felt like hacking away at moving targets that seem to hit you every now and then.  No challenge and no excitement.  The bosses are just higher hp and armored foes whose ai is just as terrible.  I'm not claiming to be a great player, but I know that I'm not a bad one and if I'm just hacking at moving targets disregarding my own hp it just feels like tedious clicking to finish the mission.
This game is still quite fresh so it doesn't have a big player base, but at this rate it feels like it never will.  I'm not sure how I can help to promote this game as no one really cares about some random dude on the internet.  I've told friends and they said it doesn't look that great even though I think it has the potiential to be.  Hopefully it will catch on.
There is a mechanic everyone seems to be in agreement of hating.  The groggy mechanic.  It's only purpose is allowing for enemies to perform a finisher move on you.  Sure the finishers look quite satisfying, one even has you grab the enemey by the neck and show them off as your prey before killing them.  But, that is all it is there for.  Which is annoying, if a player hp is low enough I think just being able to perform the finisher on them is good enough.  Get rid of the groggy mechanic, you're forced to mash the r button and stand there like a drunk idiot.  Just let us strive for our survival with a sliver of hp, not button mash r.
You can improve your aresenal of attacks by leveling them up: requiring money, points, and reaching a certain level.  But, for some reason it doesn't show to be of any benefit at all for me.  I hover over it and it still says it does the same damage and require the same amount of stamina.  I haven't seen any improvements on my attacks using the same gear I used previous to leveling up my attacks.  And I can't test if they do, do more damage.
Pros
- Fighting mechanic
- Graphics
- Players
- Progressive Player Building
Even with all the cons I have listed, I still think this is a great game and has potential to grow to an even better game.  The fighting mechanic is fluid and fun.  Where timing and precision is a must.  A certain weapon has a more fine hitbox requiring you to think about if you should try that next attack or not.  Performing finishers is always fun as you it's a way to gloriously say hey I wanted to kill you and now I'm going to.  The fighting mechanic alone outweighs the cons for the most part as it's the reason why I play this game.  I wanted to play a game that was pvp with close quarter combat weapons.  This game filled that want.  The graphics are quite nice, showing great details in the maps, armor, and weapons.  The textures aren't anything to write home about, but you can tell that the developers do care for aesthetics.  The players I've come across are usually the top of the scoreboards.  They've played the game for awhile and know how to have fun.  A certain few have been ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s ,but mainly I've encountered friendly respectful players.  If you're stuck 1 v 2, they will take turns in fighting you. (for the most part)  The equipments are what will make the biggest difference.  Kind of like giving a novice a gun vs a master archer.  It's noticable in combat and just having one equipment could be all the difference you need in a close fight.
I've thoroughly enjoyed this game, and will continue to do so.  I think everyone should give it a try as it is very fun.  Taunting at the big leagues and fighting them to a close deathmatch to only be stabed in the back of another enemy player is always annoying, but enjoyable at the same time.  The game itself is fun and the players are the factors that can improve that or make it less enjoyable.  I do recommend this game and think it's worth that $15 price tag.

The thumbs down is more from frustration than an actual dislike of the game. The presentation is beautiful and its built on a fantastic core game, but after nearly two years, the AI is still ridulously stupid. Although it is "fun" to play, solo games frequently devolve into a tedious end game, and you're often given way too much time to catch up when the AI could and should be pushing for the Crown of Command. Instead of going for the win, however, the AI prefers to diddle around turn after turn rather than enter the scary portal. Sometimes it goes in, and goes right back out on its next turn. Huh?
An example of poor decision-making:
In the early game, the Wizard, who can choose to make a battle it initiates Strength or Craft based, has built up an amazing 10 Strength to go with its inherently strong Craft score. Another AI player casts the "Random" spell on the Wizard, who rolls a 2, which would make him lose all that bonus Strength. The Wizard, who has a full 3 Fate points available to re-do a roll, chooses to lose all his extra strength (dropping him to 4) rather than spend a Fate point to re-roll.
I've also seen the AI cripple itself by dropping extremely good items to hold onto 4 Talisman cards, when none of the other players are even close to ready to go for the win. These weaker players then grab those good items, making them competitive, whereupon they beat up the formerly strong AI player and wrest Talisman cards from him.
I could write pages more of examples like these, but I don't want to bore you. Just know that every solo match is flled with poor AI decision-making like this. It gets frustrating, and makes games last a lot longer than they should. Completing a vanilla game with more than 4 total players takes forever.
I haven't tested the multiplayer, but as a platform I'm sure this would be great at a LAN party if you didn't want to bring out or didn't have the boxed games.

POP: Methodology Experiment One
I first came across this game looking for a new profile background. When I saw this [art piece] I was interested to find out just what it was all about. After buying it and trying to figure out just what to be doing I started to kind of get it. Then I found and option to turn on commentary to learn just what I had finished.
This is not a game for everyone.
4/10 Gameplay: It's short and confusing if you don't know how to play it.
9/10 Style: It's got style for days.
I highly suggest the in-game commentary option. It felt like I was taking a gallery tour.

What is POP: Methodology Experiment One ?
Genre: adventure, told in different, non-canonical scenes
Setting: different 20th century themed scenes, both famous and common, to be travelled by the player
Difficulty: 0/10 --> you progress, no matter what. 9/10 if going for achievements
Length: about an hour for a single playthrough
Mode: singleplayer campaign, replayable "vignettes" (=scenes)
The positive aspects:
- different scenes from 20th century's history, such as manned spaceflight, mignight air raid, boarding a helicopter in a war territory
- strange scenes mix with bad resolution videos and lets you guess what the story or moral of the game could be (This could also be on the negative side, though)
The negative aspects:
- Horrible controls. In some scenes, you don't know if pressing keys does affect the game at all
- The options menu is no use at all. rebinding keys does not work
- Loading times. For just a small scene, it can take a modern computer up to half a minute to load
- General slowness. Press a button for two seconds to continue here, press it for six seconds to continue there. Seriously: WTF?!
- No storytelling, no moral, no underlined questions, no nothing.
- Considering these aspects, getting all achievements will become a tough challenge, to say the least
Result (and summary for those who have no time reading):
POP's an art game designed by some art-related guy for art students primarily. At least that's what it felt like for me. Actually, being an enthusiastic player of games with a little weird spin, playing it didn't enrich me at all. Plus, short length, screwed controls and loading times impair the playing experience negatively.
Thus I do not recommend buying this game at all.

The game is an accurate conversion of Fantasy Flight's revised 4th Edition, with all the content, and more. AI opponents are continuing to improve as the game develops, offering a good challenge when no-one is available to play online. Online multiplayer works well, and offers gamers like myself the opportunity to play against like-minded folks from across the globe. Gameplay is generally quite simple but with many strategic nuances the game can be played over and over again, and should continue to keep players interested with hopefully frequent updates containing the expansion packs.

The little blurb describing the game promises almost a ridiculous amount and boy does it deliver. This game is evidently still in early days yet, as noted by the alpha tag and in terms of additional content, but the core gameplay loop is there and it's wonderfully varied. The character unlock system is fluid and very fun, you always have a refreshing amount of options in terms of playstyles and it's fun in and of itself to unlock the new classes, which create sort of gimmick runs (completing a level with only your fists/undetected etc). Want to be a gorilla fist fighting and lunging everything? Sure. Want to be a thief and stealth about, teleporting into walls and getting in and out before anyone notices? Sure. Gang member inciting turf wars? These are all things many games promise but the execution of Streets of Rogue is spot on, it actually delivers this.
The music is great, the aesthetic is great and it feels very satisfying to play each character class as they were intended. This game is as fast paced or as slow and tactical as you like.
Overall, very impressed and this is coming from someone who has a hard time enjoying roguelikes.

If I'd like to tell long story short, I'll say that game is really nice, total rate is 8/10. But to be honest, from first game of series only hidden balde, stealth-mode, hood and entire-game long dream to revenge have left.
If I'd like to tell every criterion one-by-one, I'll say that:
1) Graphics and entire game world 10/10
2) Big objects physics 9/10
3) Small objects physics 5/10
4) Did I really wanted to get through all game? 8/10
5) Main characher story, also other people stories 9/10
6) Did I really wanted to get 100% after completing main story? 2/10
7) Fighting and synthetic intelligence 5/10
8) In game and real life history matching 9/10
And now about all of that criterions:
Graphics are really awesome. No lags, no freezes and other stuff like that on ULTRA-preset. Really beautiful surroundings, animals, cities, deserts etc. And all of that is in really HUGE world. Can't even understand how had Ubisoft done that in 4 years.
Big objects physics is well-made. I've got only one bug with horse in my 22-hours long game. Horse just became mad in one moment and flew away like in space.

By small objects I mean clothes, touching etc. I've got like have of a million times, when some parts of my outfit went crazy and just started flying. Hands felt inside other bodies really often. And a lot, no, A LOT OF OTHER THINGS. Those things looks really ugly for me
Main quests were really interesting BUT (!!!) you sometimes you can't join main quest because your level is too low to do it, and you have to do secondary quests. And like half of the secondary quests were so boring, in which I had to get on other side of a map, kill 2 000 000 enemies, get one piece of bracelet, get back and understand, that I forgot to loot this piece from dead enemy. 12/10 of really interesting side quests.
Despite of the fact, that we starts game without any info about main character, after completing entire game player understand all of things, that he haven't knew. That +1 point for level of interest of main quests.
When you've done main quests and kill of the bandits, you won't play any more in AC:Origins because of boring side quests. You may just enter the game for like 30-40 mins, but after that you'll fall asleep.
Fighting system is retOrded. Definitely retOrded. You have to use only 3 buttons to kill everyone in that game. Awesome, interesting, alluringly. Fighting system is same retOrded as a synthetic intelligence. When you killed an enemy, no one of his (enemy's) friends will notice that. Also you may hide in 2 millimeter-tall grass and no one will see you.
Really amazing Cleopatra's and Caesar's pictures. Cleopatra looks like real one (wanted to get some balls inside her for entire quests around her ( ͡° ͜ʖ ͡°) ). Also you may see that Caesar were killed in same way as same called salad was cut. Noice.
I really like that game, with considering all of that bad sides. And yes, I'm not a big fan of open-world games, this game is 4th in that type of games. So don't appraise my review so hard.

**********UPDATED******* Found fix for my constant crashing issue! Thanks for the help guys, least it was 1 of the simple things that fixed it. lol
-Was as simple as disabling ALL forms of Vsync (in game and forcing it off in AMD Radeon settings.
-I have a 75hz monitor, so I also had to force (in Radeon settings) to put a FPS cap of 60 on this. Running it over 60 FPS causes instabilities Iguess.
This game is a small gem though. I love and adore the Half-Life series and this I feel is very true to how it would actually be as an RTS.
That being said, it's not without its flaws/bugs. But I am enjoying its story, nonetheless, seeing more (not badly done) Half Life content is always a plus!
Pros
-Sticks to lore very well. All events and troops etc are lore friendly, fit well and execute well together.
-Story: The few singleplayer missions there are, I really like. They fit the feeling and are fun to do (until difficulty becomes stupid - see cons)
-Simple RTS. I view this as a positive since some RTS's have so much units, counters, research etc that make it a chore for newcomers to try, let alone manage all the different units into counter groups, make them fight effective units (you get my point I think)
Has a handful of units that are very clear what their good at, and when you have them fight what they aren't ment to counter, they still do decent, not just instantly die horribly like other more complex RTS's.
-Vort antlion spam. Best defense/harrasment ever and very satisfying. xD
Cons
-Difficulty.
Good luck beating any of the story missions on Normal or Hard (aside from 1st mission).  The AI will rush you fast with very powerful units before you even can get 1-2 control points OR have enough time to even get some troops trained to counter them. It's.. kind of insane. It sucks, since having it on Easy makes them nearly ever attack you.  Granted, this is more of a multiplayer mod it seems which dissapoints me.. I love the 3 missions I've done so far in singleplayer and hope to see more along with the AI modified for Normal/Hard.
-Buuugs.
Enemy units like to sometimes teleport below ground, where they can attack you and your buildings, but you can't touch them, even with explosives. This is remedied by having 1 weak troop stand on top of the stuck unit, then they just dance with each other never shooting. lol
-Troop AI needs improvement on grouping/pathing. Lot of times mine would keep running straight into my turrets and take sometimes a full minute to correct themselves and try to walk around the side of it.
(This also causes a lot of issues trying to get out of AoE attacks fast. Hard to do because of this. It is also insanely hard to make all units stay in defensive spots and not move, and next to impossible to make them all sit in a building together after having very few in it.)
-No way to save your game. At all.
Most of my complaints are things that can be fixed with polishing it up (mostly - I hope they get more campaign missions and a save feature) So, it isn't bad.
I am hopeful for this and hope it fleshes out into a good game, and maybe moved to a better engine (if possible) to allow for steamworks mod support.. That would breathe a lot of good life into this I feel.
I just hope it doesn't crash constantly for whoever reads this and tries.. but,  least you can try my solution if it does!

I used to stay as far away from them as possible, and this game still managed to win me over.

This is one of those meta-sim-sandbox-edu-tutorial-discovery games that are so common these days, but it's still tough to explain what you can actually DO, if not what it actually IS, so let me try to explain with a brief anecdote.

Years ago, my kids wanted a dog.  They begged for some unspecified period of time, until one day we were driving along and saw a 'free puppy' sign at a farm.  We stopped, and wound up taking home what the farmer told us was a 'purebred Welsh Olive Hound'.  Thing is, when we took it to the vet for shots, we found out it was actually a toaster oven.
I guess what I'm trying to say is that Universe Sandbox looks like a game, but it's a lot more like a toaster oven.  Everyone should have one, but it won't be fetching you any sticks.

Main game:
While this game is not the most 'loved' iteration of the Assassin's Creed franchise, I actually enjoyed it. You do notice that the game is less polished since I encountered some weird glitches from time to time. None of them were game breaking and my game crashed only once - although I do not know whether that was AC3's fault or just my computer.
DLC - Benedict Arnold:
This was a neat addition to the game, offering some extra story and content but it wasn't all too special. Just some extra missions which do not take very long. Get this only on a sale if you want to.
DLC - Tyranny of King Washington:
This DLC I really enjoyed! It's a unique experience very different from the actual main game in terms of gameplay mechanics. I got this DLC when I bought the Deluxe edition on a sale, but I definitely recommend buying this DLC for those who have the standard AC3 game! The only two things that bothered me in this DLC were:
1) there are chests and treasures literally everywhere! At first, I collected them all - which took quite a while - but then I actually noticed that they are not useful at all. They offer upgrades to the quiver and pistol and give you ammo, but I did not use those very often in the game;
2) the 'save citizens' / 'attack convoys' etc. challenges were very easy to farm and redo in order to get a 100% sync, but they kept popping up if you had already succesfully executed enough of them. Moreover, the attack convoys sometimes glitched, where their guards were sort of rubber banded when you performed an air assassination on them.
Other than that: GREAT DLC!

FRUSTRATING!
The main missions are too easy to the point of being rediculous. The optional objectives are difficult to the point of impossible, the controls are very random.
If you want 100% completion, hope you like watching the same unskippable cutscenes over and over again for a two second chance to push the correct button.
The side missions are fun and the game is quite educational (I live in Boston and have learned a lot of new things), but I don't know if I can stomache to finish it.
UPDATED: I did in fact finish it, and, in retrospect, it wasn't THAT bad, although I probably won't be playing it again any time soon.

"I landed near the Greek city state of Heraclea and set my camp 10 stadia from the settlement. Envoys from greek and italic city states that wanted to be liberated from Roman oppression came to me with offers of fealty, supplies and men. My Tarantine allies warned that a roman army was marching against me, coming from the northwest path near Beneventum. Their leaders was senator Valerius and general Mus. Senator Valerius has funded the expedition, hoping that a triuph against a "barbarian" invader will win a re-election in the Senate and possibly an officio authority. I decided to leave back in my camp the War Elephants, the Celts mercenaries and some other infantry units and march to meet the enemy in a field of my choice. I took with me the core of epeirotes Heavy Phalangites, 5 regiments of 2750 men force each one, 2 regiments of mercenary Hoplites, 2 companies of Xistophoroi (heavy cavalry) , 3 companies of thessalic Armoured Cavalry and 5 loose formations of light infantry (javelin throwers and archers most of them). I formed 3 regiments composed from the men that my allies have offered me and with a march formation we traveled towards the enemy."
"After one day and a half my scouts reported that the enemy army was close to our position and that we will meet them soon. I chose a field with plains and some hills and forests in south side. On my left flank i formed the phalangites to a wide line and trusted the command on my third son Orestes.Their orders were to close the enemy at half pace in order to meet them on the plains and make full use of the 7 meter long sarissa pike. My right flank was a hilly area and for that reason i put the Italic Allies with the support of the merc hoplites close behind them. I took command of the Thessalic cavalry in the center of the formation behind the infantry line while Chrysanthos took command of the Xistophoroi. The Romans were coming in wide diamond formation with mixed regiments of hastati and principes being the first line, triarii in the second line and Italic Allies and raw recruits forming the third line. General Mus was leading in the front along with a veteran regiment while Senator Valerius was in the second line with the only Equites (medium cavalry) regiment present in the roman formation. I ordered Crysanthos to make a flanking move behind the hills on the right side of the battlefield and charge Valerius and his cavalry. The right flank will take a defencive stance on the top of the hills while my phalangites on the left flank will get close to the enemy on a slow march. The gap between the two flanks will let some space for my cavalry to charge and disengage when the opportunity arise. That was the general battle plan...but Gods forgive me for being arrogant and overconfident...i didn't take account of the unknown back then to me Roman war ethos."
"The battle started favorably for me. After some skirmishes between the light infantry, the romans charged against my phalangites formation. We won several clashes and the pikes repelled many times the roman infantry. General Mus charged the first in the center of the field, regiment in order to support the latest attack of his men. That was a chance for me and my cavalry to join the battle and march through the gap, attacking the flanks of the General's regiment. But before i could make my move a messenger came to me and reported that the situation on the right flank was dire. The Italian Allies units were in full dissaray and two of them were routed from the hills. The mercenary hoplites regiments were marching quickly to cover them but they were fighting now an uphill combat against a wider formation, composed by romans veterans, the triarii. I took two cavalry companies with me and left the other behind to support the phalangites formation. The situation when i arrived on the right flank was getting worse. All my Italic regiments were routed and the hoplites regiments were fighting a losing battle. The only good news were that Chrysantos had attacked and killed the senator Valerius but his company was chasing the retreating Equites while the other Xistopohoroi company was bogged down in combat with two Roman regiments. I quickly made a prayer to all mighty Zeus and ordered my men to charge."
"The combat was frantic and neither side could gain the upper hand. My hoplites fought valiantly, despite the fact that they were mercenaries, and stood against a more numerous enemy. My charges managed to drive some Roman regiments away but the triarii were fighting like lions. After many clashes the hoplites were starting to loose morale and falter and my cavalry regiments had took too many losses. The Romans renewed their attacks and two fresh regiments of raw hastati took part in the combat. All seemed lost. Me and my bodyguards were fighting for our lives, one hoplite regiment routed and after a while the other Thessalic company routed too. We were fighting alone..."
"Suddenly a horn sounded and a big cavalry mass attacked the romans from behind. It was Crysanthos and his Xistophoroi, finally coming back to the main battlefield. First the hastati regiments started to rout and after some time the triarii gave all hope and fall back. My men were decimated and only 100 were still alive (from a force of 650). I let Crysanthos to take care of the retreating enemies in the right flank with the help of some light infantry units and i marched to the other side of the battlefield to find what was the situation there. To my satisfaction the phalangites formation remained solid and had drive many enemy regiments away from the battle. Even general Mus had retreated."
"It was a victory. But a very bitter kind of victory. I lost 45% of my men (killed and wounded) while Romans lost 60%. IT WAS A PYRRHIC VICTORY after all."
If you want to live the same emotions give this game a try. It wont dissapoint you.

First, I bought this off of the Slitherine website. Activated my key # per Steam so that I could write a review.
This game is awesome, pure & simple. If you are a fan of turn based warfare games, particularly of miniature war-gaming...this is a must have. This game, as early as it is, has no noticeable flaws & will only get better because of the very engaged devs & a tremendous, very active, community per the Slitherine & Matrix Games forums.
This game has much to offer historian buffs from this time period to include modding & scenario designing. PLUS it has the traditional PBEM multiplayer & my favorite...true "hotseat", which works wonderfully. This game really shines as a multiplayer past-time. This is one Early Access game you should avoid, at least for the time being. The content in the game currently lasts all of 15 minutes, and none of it is any good. There are far better platformers out there with far fewer flaws.
First of all, one of my pet peeves surfaces in this game: it doesn't recognize the d-pad. For a platformer that specifically tells you to use a controller every time the game loads, this is borderline unforgivable. The platforming itself feels boring and uninspired, consisting of short levels with not much to do in them. Sometimes the jump decides it isn't going to jump today. The timing on getting a boosted jump from springs feels similarly capricious. The random level generator usually spits out unplayable garbage, and the actually developer-designed levels are so sparse as to barely be worth mentioning. The level select resets to the first level every time instead of automatically moving to the newly unlocked level, which is a minor annoyance.
In its current state, there is nothing that should compel you to spend $10 on this game. In fact, if you wait you'll actually get a
price, unlike most Early Access games which offer you a discount to encourage you to buy an incomplete product:

TRIPPY: RETRO: EXPERIMENTAL: SOUNDTRACK
Many don't know this, but POP is a game from another dimension. Really. I'm not kidding.
Often on sale for under $2 or even $0.99, buying POP is a no brainer for fans of video games who appreciate creativity, experimentation, interactive experiences, and wild aesthetics, as well as great music and sound design. Actually, the music is better than great.
Fans of trippy games or interactive experiences should absolutely get this without a second thought. Yes, it is short. I guess a first playthrough took me about 20 minutes, but it is a memorable experience and has great replayability. It's an immersive 20 minutes to say the least. You will be entertained, perplexed at times, and surprised. I've never played anything else like it .
To put it simply, the game has 7 minigames sandwiched between interesting imagery and short video montages. It is up to the player to figure out how to play the minigames. And for a few, the objective isn't even readily apparent.
You'll be dropped into a boat during a thunderstorm, a highway car race, a war helicopter, a walk in the desert, a space shuttle launch, and a game similar to Missile Command. The presentation of the games is very pixelish and retro. Even outside of the minigames, pressing certain keys will affect music and artwork. The main menu itself is an exercise in interactive experimentation. The music is FANTASTIC.
I got the game on sale for over a dollar I think. It is always on sale. But, for real fans of this sort of thing, the full price of $3.99 is very reasonable. It's the price of a fancy cup of coffee or a beer. This will stay with you long after playing just once. I've played this at least 5 times and still notice new things. Did I mention the OST?
The C64 demo scene still has more to offer than this thing ever hopes to accomplish.

It goes without saying, but don't play this game if you suffer from photosensitivity.
I'm not sure that POP really classifies as a game.
There is no coherent story, and only small segments of scenes that actually have a gameplay element to them, and even there it doesn't surmount to much. That said, this game wouldn't be out of place in a modern art gallery. It would fit right in there. It is very abstract, i guess.
The controls work with either a keyboard or a controller. And it is worth noting that while at the start it says hold anything, not just any button works.
The music in some of the playable scenes is ok.
I wouldn't even recommend this game if you're a fan of "games that aren't really games", as this just flies right off the scale.

Honestly, I can't recommend this game at all. Yes I have a lot of time on it, yes the base game is enjoyable, but the developer is just such an idiot that it makes the game painful to try to enjoy.
- The text box for characters is awful and despite a billion people crying out for him to fix it, he refuses to. The text doesn't even make sense either once it's repeated 10 times in a row.
- Combat feels clunky. You want to chug those potions to save your♥♥♥♥♥ right? Well, you gotta get out of combat mode and mindlessly hop around to actually do that without being able to fight back.
- Multiplayer is absolutely broken. You thought it looked really nice on that video up there, right? Well it's not. Multiplayer comes with a billion bugs. If you are the host, suddenly most effects in the game become broken or just don't work altogether. It was so badly implemented. It's sad when you look at the game's wiki and see.. "DOES NOT WORK IN MULTIPLAYER. EFFECT DOES X IN MULTIPLAYER. IF YOU ARE HOST, EFFECT DOES NOT WORK" next to so many items and augments.
- Speaking of augments, a couple of them are bugged and don't even work properly. Yes, main customization features for your character are bugged out and were never fixed. Logic.
- The unlockables are restrictive and anti-fun, especially when they REQUIRE you to sack off your character that you had just spent hours on. Yes, you grind for hours, suicide, hope to hell you just managed to unlock that "50% chance" reward.
- Death in the game makes you want to punch your laptop. Seriously, it never feels justified. It's always over things like "I got pinned by an enemy and couldn't get out because of the thin map design despite 'boss' enemies being huge" or "I touched an enemy once and he stacked up over 100% burn damage that deals half my HP in damage per second."
- Missions are painfully dumb. You go from "collect 100 of x useless item that any level can do" to "you're now in an area where enemies can easily one-shot you past level 50" with no degree of warning that you're about to suicide.
- Back to unlockables for a second, y'know those missions I just mentioned that are painfully dumb? Well, when you get to the end of the (lol.. 15 minutes tops..) super intensive quest line, you're faced with a (pretty unfairly) powerful boss. Your reward for beating them? A cosmetic reward that you can't actually see when playing the game. Yes, you just beat some of the hardest enemies in the game for cosmetic head-gear that's overrided and hidden right from level 1 the moment you put on a helmet. Nope, no way of swapping the overlay of items like in other games. You just make your character lose out on perks for nothing.
- Certain elements of combat are nonsensical. If you get pinned by a boss and your character doesn't move (pinning yourself between it and a wall), suddenly you become invincible and can freely kill it because the developer thought it was a smart idea to "fix" the pinning problem in that fashion. Oh, but wait, that actually doesn't fix you still being pinned because you can't bypass the monster until it's dead. You're just given an exploitable immunity for.. no reason.
- The early portion of the game was so poorly designed that the developer implemented an item that costs absolutely nothing in resources that gives you 5 MINUTES OF 50 PERCENT (%) DAMAGE REDUCTION. I can go and craft 1,000 of that item for the hell of it and always have 50 percent damage reduction for all of my game time with no time required to obtain it all. Why the hell is that a thing? That's an end game kind of item that's OP in almost any other game out there, but I can get it in bulk casually at level 1.
- Selling items to a vendor gives back "credits" (currency) in values that make absolutely no sense. Developer broke the game at one point by making a useless exploitable item give you free stacks of credits, but he reverted the change and instead just made a bunch of items worthless again as opposed to properly fixing the problem.
- Some weapons are undeniably useless and 'combat chips' (combat abilities) feel royally unbalanced. There should be a fun factor, then a useful factor. The developer managed to avoid both with many of the weapons to the point where there is never any excuse to use them over others. As for the combat chips, some are unbalanced in comparison to others (again, no excuse to use certain ones) and their mana costs are a bit nonsensical. The developer ♥♥♥♥ed them up before and made mana costs too low in conjunction with an augment, but instead of applying any proper fix, he just cocked up the mana costs and nerfed the augment instead.
- Sound effects were never added for certain weapons despite them desperately needing them. Many of the current sound effects sound nonsensical and poorly downloaded from somewhere online.
- Items were never given fun or amusing effects despite the game desperately needing it. Most of them are rehashed from one another and given tiny, tiny quirks. Melee items are painfully ineffective and most just opt out for the couple of melee-based items with ranged effects.
- Quests aren't marked with any kind of indicator or (!) to let you know who you're even supposed to speak to. Easy to figure out, but still feels like bad design.
- The levels aren't even randomly generated yet still have poorly designed black box areas and abrupt ends to the map that you can see past.
- The developer has nothing in mind for the game. He ditched mid-development and came back to say "here's some 5 minute pixel art in the form of new characters (that are so brainlessly simple to balance that calling this an update doesn't even make sense)." Meanwhile none of the actual game-ruining bugs have been fixed and none of the poor design choices have been touched.
If you can ignore being frustrated with every element of this game, then it's a 10/10 gem enjoy.

This is a roguelike in the Rogue Legacy or Darkest Dungeon sense, where you build up a base outside of the game that helps you complete your runs. You'll repeat the same areas over and over to get better loot. The RPG system in the game is very simplistic - one stat will contribute towards your damage, vitality gives HP, and the rest generally do very little.
Most of the weapons in the game are just the 5 or 6 basic weapon types but with different particle effects and damage numbers.
Lastly, because you can loose your hard fought loot by dying, you are pushed towards repeating very easy areas often instead of wanting to try harder ones. It's a frustrating game loop of grinding and levelling up.  The core gameplay is decent, at least, but not worth the meh that surrounds it.

Talisman is the great board game from the 80's.  I grew up with it, I played it forever, and I missed it until now.  The digital edition is brilliant.  It has all that the board game had without all the mess and setup.
Tali DE has full online multiplayer capability, so you are able to play with up to 3 other players or NPCs.  You gain experience that unlocks special runes to enhance your starting abilities as well.
The DEVs are working constantly on improvements and additions.  All the original expansions and characters are being added piece by piece.
The game is part luck of the dice, and part RPG.  Your character has certain abilities depending on what class it is, and you can pick up tons of items, magic items, followers, and spells throughout the game.  You will do battle with enemies, ghosts, and other player characters as you journey to the crown of command... then use it to kill everyone else in game!  The game has also recently added some alternate endings, so you now have a choice of what wins the game.
Highly recommend if you like casual games with a hint of chess..  Fun but tacticle.

First I have to say the most important thing is that 95%+ of the population has not beat this game as of a couple months of this game being released. The game is extremely difficult even on Angel Mode (Easy) for a majority of players, and Mortal Mode (Regular) is much more difficult. Take into account this game was made by the person who made 'I wanna be the Boshy' which is known as one of the most notoriously difficult games to date.
With that said, this game is absolutely stunning.
* The Controls are great, they are very responsive with both a keyboard and controller.
* The Music is fantastic, I ended up buying the Album and I rarely buy music, Ashton Morris definitely put his heart and soul into his tracks.
* The games length is quite long, and with the difficulty it will give you many of hours of fun (and agony). Every boss is very unique and most of them are very difficult so expect to die a lot until you get their attack patterns memorized.
* There are quite a lot of secrets in the game which all give you garments your character can wear, also defeating bosses and getting achievements earn you them too. There are also several hidden weapons to find in the game, though are not needed to complete it.
* The story is decent, nothing extremely special but I didnt jump into this game expecting a deep story but it gets the job done. Pretty much 'kill the bad guy save the world' kind of deal.
Here are my bad experiences with the game.
* There are a few parts in the game that will legitimately make you angry and want to quit unless you stay persistant and learn to perfect an obstacle until you get past it. There are a few parts that require perfect timing and execution so you will die hundreds of times on some parts of the game.
* Also, the last boss is one of the most frustrating experiences I have had in a game in a very long time. Every other boss you progress further as you learn their move sets and for the most part are very enjoyable, but not the final boss. You will bash your face on it for a long time, nearly everyone I have spoken too will agree that it is not a very enjoyable encounter at all; to which many have quit and not finish the game.

So one of the selling points for this game is that it rewards skill and doesn't punish the player arbitrarily. Another is that its made by the creator of an I Wanna be the Guy-style game. You might wonder if this might contradict the first, and unfortunately it sort of does.
I haven't played I Wanna be the Boshy, but in this game at least the developer has done away with the gotcha moments of I Wanna be the Guy; what you see in the platforming segments is mostly what you get. Bosses do get extra moves later on in their fights, but that's reasonable, although there is a problem with it I'll get to in a bit.
But those of you who have played I Wanna be the Guy and other games like it know those moments aren't the only ways in which it was difficult. You often had to make precision jumps between spikes or other hazards which you wouldn't get the first or even fifth time, and sometimes under a time limit from another hazard. In that game this was helped by the Kid being a very small target.
Vi, meanwhile, is fairly large for a platforming protagonist compared to say, Meat Boy, and her hit box is quite big as a result. She's also feels clumsy to control in parts, with enemies often hitting you because there's no reliable method of avoiding them besides mashing attack to kill them before they damage you.
The game's certainly difficult, but the difficulty and skill it requires is mostly about figuring out what the developer expects you to do here. Generally each section only has one way of completing it, and you have to figure out what combination of Vi's abilities (as of this review, I have a double jump, a glide move, and a slide) will let you do that. I wouldn't mind ordinarily, but this game is stated to be inspired by Mega Man, Castlevania, and Cave Story, all of which allow the player a lot of experimentation and freedom for problem solving.
I found the first two areas generally simple enough, but in the Grotto area the difficulty spikes massively, with a few areas nearly requiring pixel perfect movements to get past instant kill traps (of which the game has many), which often just barely clip you due to Vi's size. I'm on Mortal mode, and it doesn't really feel like 'Normal' difficulty, especially so early in the game. The easy mode isn't much help there either, since getting hit by a hazard in that will still send you back to the last checkpoint, just with some damage.
I do like a lot of aspects to the game - customizing your character with stuff you get from achievements is a neat idea, and the game really shines during its boss battles, which are pretty well-designed so far. But I don't think it expects skill of its players in a reasonable manner. If you want a platformer with a female hero that does that, give They Bleed Pixels a try. But bottom line, if you don't like these kinds of games where your death count is guaranteed to go above a hundred, I'd probably give this one a pass.

This game is great. It's a fun turn based battle strategy game not to dissimilar from say shogun or Rome total war; but the combat is purely turn based and there is no campaign map (It is also historically accurate, and attention to detail in units and their abilities is well executed).  The principles you learn in total war or any wargame with large battles worth a damn will serve you well in Fields of Glory II.  I like that you make strategic decisions that affect your next battle, and that you pick some men to garrison won regions but its not at all detrimental.  This game lets every unit shine if you deploy and execute what that unit is good at.  For example use skirmishers to bait a legionaries unit into rough terrain and smash them with warband in loose formation who unhindered by the rough ground murder the Italians.  Or use light skirmishing cavalry to force charges away from your lines and delay their units while you force moral “cohesion” tests from missile casualties.  What really makes this game great is the scope of factions you can play.  I find Fields of Glory II satisfying.

Field of Glory 2 is a continuation of brilliant tactical wargame design of Richard Bodley-Scott, it’s more of improvement over Pike & Shot and Senguko Jidai rather than the first Field of Glory which was heavily based on the table top game. Pike & Shot and Senguko Jidai were my all-time favorite in the category of tactical wargame (pre- world war 1). With the new engine introduced by Slitherine Field of Glory 2 shines really well on it, the graphics and animation wise is much better than the previous games. However, the meat of this game is the gameplay, which uses historic rules in battle for each unit, point of advantages due to terrain and moral situation In addition to General presence. The game is easy to play, the interface is clear and intuitive, while the rules and calculation of units fighting is deep and complex, you only need good knowledge of time period tactical warfare or read the detailed manual to understand the point of advantages and many other rules.
Some improvement over Pike & Shot includes:
1.	Graphics and animation (new engine)
2.	Moving a whole group of units at once.
3.	Removing unnecessary phase such a shooting and merging it results during the players turn.
4.	Push back mechanism
5.	Missiles depleted over time.
6.	The campaign system
The unit variety is huge and very diverse and of course historic accurate based on their role of that time period, the campaign system is different in this one as there is no map to move your many armies with merging and splitting, rather than just moving from one battle to another based on history with a decision to be taken in between those battle. However, the design of these campaigns are great and has very interesting battles and decision to be taken and it gives the feel of being in shoe of a general of that campaign.
One last great feature is the Multiplayer which is available in most Slitherine Turn Based games the Play by Email (PBEM++) you can jump on it against human player once you get bored of already very competent AI.
In conclusion Filed of Glory 2 is a masterpiece of tactical ancient wargame, it is my favorite already and the best in the market, there is an opputunity to see different time period DLC for the game with more interesting campaigns. If you are already a fan of Pike & Shot and Senguko Jidai or the first Field of Glory games, get this one with no question, if you in general new to this system please watch the youtube to have an idea about what the game is.
Note: I won the game during the Slitherine Twitch

I remember when Total War games by Creative Assembly were praised for the authenticity and accuracy in depicting how a battle would or could play out.  They even made a TV show out of it.  The early renditions of those games very much made you feel like a general.  Those times have long since passed and now CA has turned the Total War series into an RTS more about micro management and less about tactics.
Field of Glory II lets you be that general again.  It’s everything that has been missing for me in the Total War franchise.  I don’t have a ton of time yet, but I am extremely happy with this title so far.  I have played a couple of skirmishes, but a majority of my time has been playing and re-playing the tutorials.  It is a very simple game on the surface, but once you start scratching you can see just how deep the mechanics are.
I want to mention if you buy the physical copy from Slitherine it comes with a 150 page hardcover manual.  I wish I had known before I bought my Steam copy.  I also think you can get a free Steam key with that physical copy. (I don’t know if that last part is true, but I think I recall reading it.)

This is a great game for those interested in table-top style wargames. There are a vast array of different armies and troop types to choose from, and the previous version of the game shows that there will be plenty of DLC to come.
The graphics are a vast improvement over version 1, the interface is easy to grasp and the mechanics of move, charge, melee etc are pretty straight-forward. Battles are usually long, drawn out arm-wrestles since the AI rarely makes any major mis-steps. Having the game resolve all the melees etc means a battle that would have once taken a whole day over a table with miniatures, dice and extensive rules arguments, can now be completed in an hour or two.
Whoever did the AI for this game has done a great job. The AI seems to understand the correct tactics for different troop types and will give you a run for your money. There are 6 levels of difficulty. Rather than the AI being dumbed down for the lower levels, the difficulty levels are handled by the relative amount of points available for army sizes. So, on a lower difficulty level you will have more points available than the AI. The devs assure us there are no nerfs or maluses for the AI.
There are set maps for the included battles, but you can set up practically any battle you wish, and choose a particular region, to have a map automatically generated. You get to choose your army composition - within the limits of historic accuracy - but you can have any army fight any army for a "what if" scenario.
There is a basic campaign mechanism (no map) which allows you to fight with the same force, build their experience, re-enforce them, etc. Because of the points based system it would be possible to run your own campaign, where battles are resolved in FoG II.
On-line multiplayer is done via email notifications that it's your turn. Face-to-face is done via hotseat.
I haven't discovered any bugs yet, no crashes, it does not need a lot of resources - I can run it fine on my surface pro core M3.
The price is more than fair: it's a definite bargain. But is it fun? Absolutely. Every single battle I've played, even the tutorials, are riveting. I've never saved a game half way through because I can't stop once I've started.
I have been playing wargames - both table top and board and computer - for forty years, and this is once of the best games I've experienced. Bonus: the devs listen and are active on the Slitherine forum and here. RBS is a well regarded game designer and communicates well with wargamers. He's one of us.
I would have liked a map based campaign, but for the price I think the game delivers beyond expectations. Ten out of ten.

The concept of Streets of Rogue is an awesome one, but I'm not too sure how to feel about the game. I understand it is a rogue like game, but I see some potential to build it potentially into a RPG. Whether the devs are going for that - not completely sure. Just an FYI for my reader : I'm not a huge rogue-like type fan so games like this are usually off my radar (unless its Rogue Legacy).
Streets of Rogue is a rogue-like game. Meaning, its a game you are meant to play and not die. Once you die, you start all over again. You are, however, able to save your progress at anytime simply by quitting the game. This progress is only saved only if your character/player is still alive. If you happen to die during your adventure, it's time to start ALL over again! That's the small issue I have with this game. Although I understand the point of rogue type games, it sort of drives me nuts that I have to go sifting through a bunch of garbage bins and houses to acquire money, items and weapons. The
itself is simple and straight forward. One joystick is used to navigate while another allows you to aim your attack.
The basic premise of the game involves completing main missions on the map. This can be rescuing someone or taking someone out. Along the way, you may come across salesmen, items you can pick up or people you can hire for your cause. You can choose to fight whoever or ignore whoever. There are times you will be forced to fight as there will be no other way to complete your mission. One feature (besides beating someone up to clear a building) is you can poison the ventilation system in the building and force everyone out. Because the game is still in early access, I think there is a lot more that can be added to diversify how you would like to approach a scenario. Speaking of diversity, you are also able to choose a unique character with distinct abilities to complete your mission. Gangsters for example start off with weapons and are able to recruit other gang-members for free on the map. Each character has different endurance, strength, speed and accuracy. I can definitely respect the variety of abilities and (unlock-able) characters. The game features local co-op as well as online gameplay which is awesome.
The
follow a pixel style art. It is suitable to the game and the effects were done decently well. I hope they add a few more animations (or details) in the future. The
are okay overall. I think this domain definitely needs some improvement to make the player feel the impact they make in the game (whether its fighting others or hitting something).
Overall, the game is okay at this point. As I've said before - I'm not a big rogue-like game-type fan, but if you are I'm sure you'll enjoy it. If you want to back this game in early access I would say buy it on sale. I don't think the full-price is worth it (just yet... let's hope). I will hit the recommend button, but before I do I'd like to say PLEASE MAKE SURE YOU DO YOUR HOMEWORK ON THIS ONE! Check the updates, check the discussions, look at other reviews and see what everyone is saying too.
RATING : 6.85/10

POP: Methodology Experiment One exists as an abundantly expressive creative outlet for an individual who can't find their voice.
The pulsating lights, mesmerizing soundtrack, and relentlessly bizarre fast cuts of TV clips and weird artwork blend into beautifully incomprehensible chaos as they jump between micro-minigames while seeming to attempt to deliver some sort of message about the cultural insignificance of change. It does all this and yet the result is something remarkably hollow, like it was thrown together just to screw with people believing that it actually has meaning when in reality it's nothing more than a perplexing collection of sights and sounds.
Its handful of insignificant interactive scenes are inexplicably dull for how fast and incomprehensible they are, usually seeming to attempt to again convey a deeper meaning without any context or nuance. And there's something really compelling about that, but at the same time it mostly just had me wondering what I was supposed to take away from something so unfocused trying to deliver a heavy dialogue in a twenty minute compilation of random occurrences and five second slices of gameplay.
Maybe it all just went over my head, or I'm reading too much into something that doesn't exist. I quite frankly haven't the slightest idea.

The combat system sucks too, in my opinion. It's just not that fun and unnecessarily complicated. The toggling between combat mode and normal/harvesting mode is unnecessary and often causes me to misuse things. This problem is made even worse by Lenny's messages that really disorient you. Other than that, the combat is a bit primitive, especally with the level design.
Basically, the game seems seriously underdeveloped, almost to the point of a flash game, but even so it's somehow enjoyable for a while. However, not worth the price.
And finally, for the biggest problem of this whole game: LENNY.
Alright, there's just so much wrong with this guy, programming-wise and story-wise. Programming-wise, Lenny is bugged. His dialogues sometimes bug out and make him speak gibberish, which is just weird. Apart from that, again, his messages can only be dismissed outside of combat mode, which makes fighting unnessarily disorienting, and causes me to die a lot without me even knowing what's happening. Story-wise, who the hell is this guy? We're just sent in the game with this random blue kid directing us. We don't know who he is until we find him in the ship, hidden away in his own room, which turns out to be the cadet headquarters. What if you're not allianced with the cadets when you create your character? It doesn't matter. Lenny's still there to "help" you out. Which side is he actually on? Seems to me like his only goal is to kill you via messages.
This game has potential, but it's just not there yet.

This game is an absolute masterpiece. But I cannot, in good conscience, recommend this game for PC players.
In short, DRM protection cripples performance. The result is frequent stutters, CPU bottlenecking, and in some cases CPU overheating. My i7 6700K is pretty consistently at 80-90% CPU utilization during gameplay. While Denuvo and Uplay are well-known constants with debated performance impact, the addition of VMProtect combine to form the ultimate stress test that will bring any CPU under six cores to its knees. The game is constantly encrypting/decrypting on the fly, resulting in massive CPU utilization during the least processor intensive states (i.e. main menu or cut scenes).
Perhaps less offensive to the masses, this game does not have SLI support. While the game supports 4K and HDR (from the latest NVIDIA drivers at least), one is simply unable to enjoy the beauty of the game at a constant 60fps above 1080p unless running at low/medium settings. Open and empty areas in the desert surely will approach this framerate, but in highly populated cities
you will be lucky to break 40fps. I play at 1440p, with adjusted settings (low AA, medium character detail, etc.) and still cannot break 50fps in dense areas.
The game is simply beautiful, the open world is enormous with hours upon hours of exploration, and the gameplay is a refreshing change from the series usual formula (it is by no means the best, but certainly serviceable). You can clearly tell the developers were inspired by the Witcher formula, with rich side-quests and personal story-telling. It isn’t quite as deep or compelling as the Witcher’s story or side-quests like the Bloody Baron’s, but it is a step in the right direction. There is a lot of attention to non-story detail
. There is a lot left to the player to discover, and rewards expermientation and exploration.
I do have some qualms with the HUD options, which are fairly limited. There are no customization options, only presets. In and of itself that isn't a huge issue, but the stark jump between one and the other leave a lot of users without a favorable setup. In my case, all I wanted was to turn off tips/reminders, and there is no setting to do this without losing the compass and objective markers. It's is a fairly easy fix, but unfortunately I don't trust Ubisoft to put the attention into these details for at least a few months.
I will revise this review if Ubisoft decides to tone down a bit of the strangling DRM and/or works with NVIDIA to offer SLI support to alleviate the former.
