"The ammunition rules are suspended for some historical scenarios- such as the battle of Carrhae, where the Parthian commander had taken the precaution of bringing a large train of pack camels carrying spare arrows." PG 69 of the manual
If you appreciate historical attention to detail, real strategy and the time period of antiquity then this game is for you. A huge graphical upgrade from the first FIeld of Glory, as the map and units have terrific detail. You have the choice of several historical epic battles, a sandbox campaign and campaigns centered around a few famous generals (Ave Caesar!). The rulebook is worth a read, and the game itself is fascinating in it's complexities but doesn't seem overbearing. So far, a big thumbs up.

You probably have to be a dedicated wargamer to remember Fields of Glory, a turn-based strategy series that covered almost every era of ancient warfare. The historical scope was deep and wide, but the rules and features were shallow and anorexic... just saying. The game needed an overhaul. The graphics needed a facelift, and the gameplay and ruleset needed growth hormones. This game addresses those issues definitively.
It was a matter of bringing the game over to the Battle Academy engine, Which in my opinion is one of the most robust tbs platforms out there. It handles WW2 games, fantasy games like Hell, Sci-Fi with Sanctus Reach, and historical wargames Pike and Shot and Sengoku Jidai. I'm assuming that, like the old FoG, this game will eventually have a slew of historical skins DLC. Everything will be overpriced and never go on sale, but if you're a fan of any of the games above like me, you'll bite the hook... like me.
The mechanics and rules of the game work almost the exact same way as Pike and Shot and Sengoku Jidai, not the old FoG. It's lazy but it works. If you've played either, you won't need the tutorial. You'd also recognize the soft pastel, almost cartoony maps. The game looks much better than previous games. The rigid, boxey blob models are gone, replaced by units that shuffle nervously, taunt their foes, and continue swinging at each other in between turns. It's a Slitherine tbs that actually feels alive and breathing.
It's a straight up, left-click only tbs. You'll have a command unit with a command range, units outside of which will suffer a penalty. Units have zones of control. Once engaged in melee, units won't disengage, but will continue fighting each turn until one breaks. Victorious units may compulsively pursue routed foes, even disappearing off the map, never to be seen again...Units gain advantages and suffer penalties based on terrain and morale. Units get buffs for adjacent allies, and penalties if those allies are routed. There are bonuses for flanking, charging, and fighting on the high ground. There is no experience gain, no upgrades or leveling, and no rpg elements.
All the elements you'd expect from a good tbs are here, implemented in an approachable, almost casual way that you can enjoy without having to put down your drink or jazz cigarette. Turn based tacticians should approve. 8/10

. This game is pure RNG. Your task is to guess which one out of 3 symbols will come next, and build a high streak of correct guesses. Failing the prediction once will reset your streak.
The final achievement is to get a streak of 10. In each round you have a 1/3 = 33.3% chance to win. Your chance to get 10 correct predictions in a row is (1/3)^10 = 0.001693508%. Statistically you will need to play 3^10 = 59049 rounds to get a streak of 10. Doing a geometric distribution with p = 1-(1/3), statistically you get an expected value (= average streak) of 0.5 correct picks. The game takes about 4 seconds to reveal if your prediction is correct. So statistically you will need (1+0.5)*4 = 6 seconds in average to complete one round; so to complete 59049 rounds you would need an average of 59049*6 = 354294 seconds (= ~246 hours = ~10.25 days) to complete the game (as in: get all achievements).
So yeah, is it a great game concept to have a game that literally is pure RNG and will take you an average of 246 hours of active clicking time to 'complete it'? Hell, no.

Great start to a great classic game. I've been an owner of multiple versions of Talisman over the years and was very exicted to see this being worked on. While it has some bugs and annoyances, overall I think it's a great start. I'll go over some of the issues first.
1) Random crashes. Yeah , they happen. Hopefully they clear up before it goes live as this completely ruins a live game.
2) Bad network connectivity. People randomly just disconnect. Whats worse, is there is no way to re-join a game (that I am aware of) to continue. AI takes over.
3) Spell casting is not intuitive. I played for over a month until i realized I can queue up a spell to automatically cast on the next players start of turn. Casting counter spell at the right time seems rough. The general responsiveness of double clicking spells is bad. Sometimes you have to click 20 times for it to actually work.
4) No way to stop zooming into the board. This might be good for most people are a new to the game, but veterans dont need to read the board every time and would rather keep an overall look of the board. They need to make this an option.
Other than these three issues, the game is great. The rules are handled very well, I have only found one or two issues I have had to report on rules. The animations dont overbear the game. The speed of turns is just right, with included features like auto-kill when there is no need to roll opposing dice.
One feature i'd like to see is allowing AI to play your turn for you while you take a bathroom break :)

~CONS~
Race and Gender locked classes. Decide on a class first and work from there.
Yes there is that one loli-looking race
The action combat requires a better internet connection than WoW-like games due to dodgeing and blocking.
Low-End systems beware, some of the minimum settings can cause foes to render after they have been hitting you
The single bank tab is on the small side, and is shared across all charaters on that server.
Crafting can be S L O W to grind.

After 70+ hours and countless side-quests later, I can finally say that this game just doesn't ♥♥♥♥ing end. When a new AC-title comes out I always jump on it with little to no hype and no high expectations. I just play the story and... Done! I went in on AC Origins the exact same way. And I usually complete the game within 24 hours of playtime. However, after about 6-7 hours of gameplay, I started to understand that this is no ordinary AC-title. It actually shocked me how much more RPG alike the series has become.
I hadn't really taken a full look at the game map until about 6 or 7 hours in. And that was when I fully understood that this is so much more than a story-based game. Upon discovering that I also got introduced to the leveling system. It kind of forces you sometimes to explore the world more and thus leading to more side-quests!
What I also love about the game is that is so damn versatile! You can hunt resources to craft better armor and weaponry upgrades, here and there you may find some minor unmarked quests and animal attacks. You want to infiltrate a for?! Fine, choose your playstyle, go full on Rambo-style or take it the sneaky way. Also, the feature of having an eagle to scout out where enemies are (and also resources) is so much more fun. It makes it easier for the player to navigate the map.
I'd like to add that this is the first AC-title I get on PC. In the past I've always got it on my Xbox 360/Xbox One because many people stated that the PC version was "unplayable" because of various bugs. I don't know if that was true, but when it comes to Origins I can't say the same. After 70+ hours of gameplay I've experienced no game breaking bug, sure I've experienced a few texture bugs here and there and my horse getting stuck in places, but nothing game breaking, no.
Lastly, I'd like to discuss the major cons of the game. As for the game itself I can only strongly recommend it to anyone who wants to play a new AAA-title this fall/winter. However there is one major con. System requirements. I run on a very powerful rig, a 1080Ti GPU and a i7-4690K CPU. It should according to the system requirements be enough. However I've still experienced major FPS-drops (mostly in cutscenes), although this might only have to do with unopitimized support for various drivers it still impacts the gameplay experience. For those with not as powerful rigs you should take the requirements with a grain of salt.
In conclusion. The game is awesome. However the requirements for the game is above what many have and even if ones requirements go over that there might be some FPS-drops. 9,5/10.

First off - I really like this game. A lot.
The devs seem really great. They respond quickly to threads and pay attention to what the players want.
That being said, I can't recommend the game in its current state (and keep in mind, I'm writing this review in Early Access. I'll update this review as things change.)
The progression system (leveling up, unlocking skills, and obtaining more powerful, upgraded weapons) is completely borked. It provides a very unfair advantage to players that have been playing longer and it's quite obvious. This ruins balance and makes the game more about who has better gear rather than who can play better. I personally think the entire progression system should be removed.
The game has general bugginess issues as well. People lagging and hits connecting when they've been dodged on my end, etc. I'm sure these are being worked on though.
Some characters have 1 hit kill combos that will stun lock you, but the devs are aware of this and are actively working on it.
Despite those flaws, the rest of the game is very very good. If they fix the balance and lag issues, this game would be amazing and I'm looking forward to the day that I can confidently give this game a thumbs up.

Home definitely deserves more credit than it is given by many of the negative reviews. This game probably isn't for everyone, so I don't mind some of the negative reviews, but I think if those people looked at it from a new perspective, everyone could enjoy it.
This game is a unique "horror"/mystery game, and it is so unique that maybe it shouldn't be considered horror.
If you're looking for a "mystery" genre game, buy Home.
If you're looking for a jump scare horror game, don't buy Home.
If you're looking for a game to nerd out over the true meaning of, buy Home.
If you're looking for a satisfyingly concluded game, you probably shouldn't buy Home.
If you're looking for a game that requires you to think and evaluate what you're seeing, buy Home.
Home was an enjoyable experience that I would recommend to anyone that can have an open mind. Your choices matter in a way that's a lot more important and obvious than most games, and that's the major reason for most of the negative reviews. Whether you're looking for a simple game to relax and work through or a game to 100%, Home is a great buy.

To be honest, this game isn't as fun nor is it boring: it's in the middle and that's how I'm going put my two cents into this thing called a "review'(OHHHHHHH! Calm down crowd, its just a review" "aww")
Like every other MMORPG out there, you start by making a character, selecting a class, and do the "rite of passage"(reach the level cap which varies depending on what MMORPG you're playing)to level 65. With the recent class - The Ninja, making it to that level is easy but we're not here to talk about that(at least not yet, hold you're doggone horses), we're here to talk about the game itself first.
The story is a bloody mess as you no longer start on the Isle Of Dawn anymore, characters are very uninteresting and the locations are nothing special and sadly don't stand out like they used to. The questing system is definitely the most boring part of the game as it's the "Rite Of Passage" route all MMORPG's do: kill this, collect that item, talk to this guy(or girl) only to kill more of that enemy or collect that item or talk to another person standing less than 5 feet away from them. The cutscenes are cool and the combat are obviously the high points but I'm going to be different and rip a big hole in that: 3.2.1(hole ripping time) - the combat is slow as hell and depending on what class you're playing it can either be fun(DPS classes), or boring than watching the paint dry channel(not a real channel so don't search it please)(aka Supporting Classes). The game is unbalanced as reapers, gunners, and Ninjas(all being gender AND race locked)being overpowered in both PVE AND PVP makes other classes(including the mandatory Healer, aka the class that's needed the most but no one wants to play)obsolute.
The dialog in the cutscenes is eye-rolling but interesting if you mute it sadly as most of what the characters said made me sleepy if it wasn't for the graphics. (hole ripping time done) You start with basic skills, as you level up you'll learn new skills which are more awesome to do. You'll also be able to do raids and dungeons for much better loot and gear(like every MMORPG out there)but waiting for a party is a time hassle because unless you're a healer/tank, it can almost take 30 minutes(to even an hour if you're like me: down on luck)to find a party. There's crafting and other stuff that I didn't care for but it's there, and other things when you're not killing something out there and♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥who PK beginners because stupidty so be careful.
My biggest problem is the classes: remember when there were no gender-locked classes and every race can be any class? Tera did a 180 and brought the brawler making it go as generic as other MMORPG's with gender-locking. Then it got worse: 2nd class(in a row)class-locked to the Eliin(a Loli who tethers on being cute and kinda creepy but we all love this class so who are we kidding. I know I did because a small character picking a huge axe is more fun) -  the Reaper. And just when one thought it couldn't get any WORSE: IT DID - 3rd class(in a row: awful I know) to add salt on a wound - The Gunner(locked to female elves). But when that class wasn't getting the attention the devs thought it should they did the most unthinkable: 4th gender locked class(painful. painful Bluehole) except it was the 2nd Elin Exclusive class: The Ninja and the final nail in the coffin for Tera.
They maybe in the green(thank you Tera)but they lost a lot of the playerbase in the progress. The game is poorly optimized as people who clearly have better PC's than I do struggle as they watch their FPS go 15fps on much better rigs says bad things indeed. And the final question of the day: would I recommend TERA to you? And the answer is simple and quick that I'll put it in captial letters for all to see in 3.2.1

I've always loved space and anything to with it, so trying out Universe Sandbox was a fun, educational experience.
If you like space and the universe, physics simulators, and experimenting with different variables in space, then you will really enjoy this game.
The aesthetics are great - it's your own solar system/galaxy/universe simulator, complete with stars, suns, etc. You can zoom in and out a great deal, and slow or speed up the real-time by a few minutes, days, years, etc. One of the coolest things to play around with is the different rings - you can add planetary rings to everything, and experiment with mass/velocity to watch how these variables influence the ring patterns. You can also toggle different colors to represent things in the universe like acceleration/velocity, mass, etc (the planetary bodies will trail different colors depending on what you select). Reflecting the realities of space, there is no sound or music, however, I didn't really mind (playing my own is perfectly fine).
The controls are simple, you just click on the variety of options available; however, understanding what each option can do may take some time to fully appreciate. The learning curve is minimal to moderate - the numerous options may itimidate people who do not understand basic physics (since this is a physics simulator in space), but the video tutorials are very helpful in getting you familiarized with each functions. There is also a list of fun things to do in the sidebar, which will offer you a step-by-step blueprint of how to achieve things like adding planetary rings to the Earth's moon and seeing how gravity effects it (very nice visuals if you try this out).
Of course, one of the first things I did while trying this out was to increase Earth's velocity and force it out of orbit - hurtling through space and turning black from freezing over. You can add moons or asteroids, turn things into black holes, and manipulate factors like velocity, mass, etc. I tried dropping moons into Earth, however, it appears to make the planet larger (as if it absorbs them). I do not know how to crash them into each other yet (or if that's even possible). With the large amount of variables you can manipulate, there is good number of things you can do and experiment with in the vastness of space.
Overall, if you have the least bit of interest in physics and/or space, then you should definitely give this game a try.
Recommend!

Having played Magicite and finishing every little thing about it, I saw all of the sudden this game on youtube. I was interested imediately. I loved Magicite and this game was playing on the same engine as it seemed. And sure enough it was even the same dev. Great! Another cool game to enjoy! To unlock things! Have some challenging roguelike gameplay! Aaaaaaaaaaaand it was kind of a let down.
Dont get me wrong. The Game is good. But looking at it from a standpoint of knowing where it came from I sadly have to say that I dislike it quite a lot. And this not only has to do with the game itself. I shall explain that further below. First lets head on in, into my experience with the games.
As I began to play Magicite I saw all unlockables and characters and pets and thought: This is going to take a long time. And it did. Not just because its hard to unlock. No. Because I was bad at that game. Having replayed a few weeks ago I seem to be quite bad at it again. So that is something. Anyways. So the unlockables where things you could get if you do specific tasks. And if you did them you would get a shiny hat, a race, a skin or even a grand little pet. And they helped you quite a lot. I most of the time use the "Mining Helmet" for more ore. But of course, that is Magicite. What about Roguelands. Did it get rid of unlockables? Hell no. Why should they? It was one grand feature. Loved it. Problem is, that they expanded on it.
Now, why in the hell would that be a problem? Lets put it this way. As an example (based on fictional values) you had 10 races in Magicite. And you have 30-40 in Roguelands (Again these numbers are just pulled out of my head, they do not represent actual numbers ingame). And these unlockables dont just stop with races. Because every race has skins. And we also have pets. Not to speak of the hats. So, where Magicite would still hard and yet enjoyable to unlock everything, Roguelands turned into a grindfest. Literally. Because that is actually how the main gameplay is, as well. Which brings me to my next point.
The gameplay in Magicite was simple. You spawn in, hack down trees, mine ore and kill mobs. All that while getting to the end of the stage. If you arent fast enough the Scourge comes in and does about 1 million damage. So, dont even try to kill it. And even if you would grind in that stage for wood and xp you would always come to an end. Because that stage is just that stage. There is no unlimited supply of wood or enemies. And while that as well stands true for Roguelands we have the problem of being able to repeat the stage an unlimited amount of times. See, in Magicite the game would push you forward. Like a true Roguelike. You cant just go back and repeat the thing to gain more items. That takes away from the challenge. Roguelands however doesnt seem to care about the challenge. It just lets you replay the stage for ressources to craft things. Which leads me to my next point.
The crafting system in Magicite was as simple as it could get. You have an inventory and from there you craft items with Shift and your mouse. Thats it. You created them instantly. Without a problem. Well, unless you screwed up and made a Greataxe instead of normal sword. A normal sword which I can fight much better with. And a Greataxe which literally screwed me over on one stage. So, yea that happened. Anyways. The crafting system in Roguelands has taken a different approach. Instead of just letting you have fun with all the recipes in your inventory and having to manage it you can go back to your own hub and store them and craft them there at various stations. So, you craft materials into badges. Similar to ore into Iron but not in a town but in your own hub. From there you craft weapons and armor. And since all need 3 badges to be complete you have a wide variety of weapons and armor. That is a quite nice idea, if it wasnt for the fact that it yet again takes away from the initial ideal challenge.
In Magicite, ressources were limited. You gained what you could see on the stages, you cannot repeat. You get into the town and look around. Do merchants sell stuff you need? Maybe a Diamond Pickaxe? Oh well maybe just a Diamond anything. Would help greatly. Hey maybe you found one in a chest on the first level! I got that lucky once. And then died. On the same level... But sadly no such things in the shop so you have to make yourself a pickaxe, an axe and a sword from the iron or stone you got. Hell, maybe you dont even have enough stone to even make a good pickaxe which leads to you not having any iron at all. So, kinda a problem. But since we are good at the game we can easily kill everything with our wooden swo- Oh god dammit it broke.
In Roguelands you can simply grind for ressources and levels. And then go back to make a better weapon. Only to then go back to the same level and grind for more. That is too easy. Especially as you only need that little robot to mine or harvest. You dont even need specifics for looting machines. Whereas in Magicite you couldnt open that golden chest without the perk. And you could only choose from two perks. So, what do you want more? Chance on great loot or do you want the chance to make big potions while making tiny potions? And as we talk about ressources, some characters/races didnt even start out with an axe or a pickaxe. Some started out with a weapon only. So you had to farm coins in the early stages and buy stuff in the later stages. In Roguelands you can just grind and craft. But how do you remember all those many craftingrecipes? In Magicite it was so simple that it was easy to remember it all. In Roguelands you have a recipe book. Granted, it is a good idea to implement for that specific feature since its quite a lot of stuff but it takes away from the challenge, yet again.
And now to the part of what I mentioned way above. The other thing that made me not reccomend the game. See, communities can be nice and can be bad. I have played Dark Souls for instance and I should know how bad communites can get. So, dont go onto the Dark Souls Forums and complain about one little thing or you will just get thrown out with everything you have. You will be denounced a casual (which seems to be an insult for these people so if someone calls you that in that community I think you have the right to be offended). Jokes aside and back to the point. Communities can be great. You can see if a community sticks together. When they play activly together, do Forum work or just have good old discussion. Or when they team up to downvote a review and harrass the reviewer because he didnt like their famous game or because they disagreed with him. Now, I dont come here and say: "Dont say mean things to me." If you wanna come over and insult me for my opinion or put up dumb arguments that focus on playtime and having to play a game longer than XX, then feel free to do so. But dont be disapointed if I flat out ignore you. The thing is just this: I dislike this game. And sadly you will have to deal with that. And since this is the fourth time that I actually write a good and more neutral review than the last one was I hope that this doesnt fall on deaf ears.

I'm actually going to write a semi-proper review for once because I believe this game deserves it however... I don't even know where to begin.
This game plays like your classic rogue-like. It's a top down RPG with a pixelated environment. It also plays like a hack-n-slash (if you so choose to take that route of relentless killing, or if you're unfortunate enough to be caught up in a riot.) There's lots of ways to play and nobody is ever going to play the same exact way as another. You can do a complete pacifist round, or you can get by with sly remote hacking. You can play as weird characters such as the midget Shapeshifter who for some reason decided being naked was completely okay, but that also comes at the price of cops attacking you on sight. That brings me to another great point.
Each character you can play as (there's many, some you have to unlock) has certain unique things about them that make them what they are. These aspects can either hinder or help your playstyle and the way you decide you want to go through each level. Some of these character traits can also be negative, causing the game to seem a little unfair, albeit hilarious, at some points.
The multiplayer is fun and actually creates more of a challenge depending on how hard headed the people you are playing with. If they aggitate a cop, said cop is also going to come after you. Multiplayer can get pretty chaotic at some points, especially when playing with a full group, but that's not really a complaint. My biggest problem with multiplayer so far has been there are no shared rewards so completing tasks feels like a race. Each level has a set of tasks you have to complete along with a reward item. These tasks vary from silly things like having to kill off the bartender to slightly annoying tasks like needing to push a bunch of buttons.
If you're playing with a group of people and you have a task to push those buttons, there may be four buttons you have to push, and you may successfully activate three, but if somebody comes along and activates the fourth then the game triggers completion of that task and they go away with all the spoils. Do you get rewarded? Nope, unless the person is generous and decides to give you the reward.
I also just want to say I think Matt is such a wonderful and talented person. There's so much he's put into this game that even whole AAA studios cannot pull off. This game deserves more than to just be called an alpha. I know there's a ton more content he plans on putting out and expanding on but Streets of Rogue really plays like a fully fleshed out game.

First of all, a word of warning: Wings of Vi is VERY difficult, and you WILL spend hours grinding away at a single boss trying to figure out how to deal with their attacks. Even the Angel Mode, the game's "easy" mode, is far from a casual experience. It's definitely not a game everyone will enjoy. If you are a fan of this genre, however, oh boy is this a treat. The game's incredible gameplay mechanics and level design are complemented by beautiful pixel art and a fantastic soundtrack.
Almost every level and every boss in the game is brilliantly designed to be challenging but fun and fair. Hardly ever is there a situation where you end up dying of random chance - death is frequent, but it's your own fault. This makes progression extremely satisfying, and every new checkpoint you reach feels like an achievement. The difficulty also curves up as you progress in the game, so that every new area and every new boss will force you to improve your skills and learn something new. The controls are tight and the combat system is satisfying.
In addition to the solid mechanics and brilliant level design there are also tons of secrets to find, more difficult modes to challenge yourself with and speedrun leaderboards where you can compare your performance with other players. The replay value is through the roof, but even if it wasn't, the experience of beating the game once is well worth buying it for.
There are some annoying glitches and lag issues that can affect gameplay in some cases, but for the most part the game runs fine. The developer is also a cool guy who listens to feedback, and he's already fixed a lot of things. Even with the occasional technical problems I would rate Wings of Vi a solid 9.5/10. It's already one of my favorite games of all time and I wholeheartedly recommend playing through this masterpiece at least once.

(For what it's worth, I've probably logged a few hundred hours on my desktop client before Tera was released on Steam.)
Honestly one of the best MMOs I ever played and the only one that I keep coming back to. I was hooked from the moment I started playing closed beta, and with constant updates like buffs to less popular classes, it just keeps me wanting more.
The combat system is a refreshing change of pace from what you see in a lot of other MMOs. Sure, it's got the grind that every other MMO tends to have, but if you can find someone to play with (easier said than done sometimes, I know!), then it becomes so much more tolerable!

Now this review may seem more negative and contradict my recommendation for this game but this is only due to what they'v been recently doing with newer updates. It's a very immersive, the character customization is not the ultimate customization tool compared to some but it has it's quirks. The game is balanced. Though when adding a new class to the game you'll usually have a few complaints on nerfing that class a bit in the next patch, for example the Gunslinger patch was a huge uproar of people demanding it to be nerfed--but this new ninja class luckily seems already acquainted with balance.
It has a huge market and trade system to entertain your time with selling and buying stuff, customizing your character without having to spend actual money (but this takes time and patience though) but it's worth it. No filters in chat, so you're technically free to say anything but i won't say no one's going to report you.
Sadly i have one, large complaint. For anyone who hasn't played Tera in the past -- before this whole 'Anya' storyline will know that the Island of Dawn was immediately the first place you'd go. It was great for basic training in every combat aspect of the game. You'd fight enemies and even go through a beginner's dungeon, it was nice. It wasn't restricted to level 65 (like it is now) and even after the Anya story, at least you would go where you need to go. What they've suddenly done after completing your quests on Stepstone Isle is send you straight to the Oblivian Woods which is not how it goes at all. You'd go to Lumbertown and do your quests in Fey forest then go to the Oblivian woods, it even says so in the level recommendations. Lumbertown is for 10-15, exactly where your level 11 butt needs to be after doing your basic training and Oblivian Woods is for 11-20, now it may look confusing but you should end Lumbertown around level 15-16 (if you focus more on main quests instead of requests or side quests) which will have you set perfectly for Oblivian Woods.
I currently have a level 42 Ninja and i'm extremely backlogged quest wise. My level is higher than even where my main quests are supposed to be and it's becoming a bore. I believe they designed this new 'system' to coddle the players and let them level higher, but this isn't fun. Some, maybe lots, will find this great but cutting off all of these beautiful worlds and never having a real challenge except for match-making dungeons, i find, is no true way to play a MMO. I want a challenge, i want to be able to enter the game and actually be excited to level up, because i know it took me a while to get the next point but with this new set-up, everything is too easy and boring. The only thing exciting left were the dungeons they'd recommend you. There's even this new Kumba game? It's very weird and new, and it probably exists for the innocent reason of having a side game--or they knew how much they ♥♥♥♥ed up the leveling system and how boring it now is they had to add a fun little game and make it a 'main vanguard request' so you'd waste your time on that and believe TERA is still good.
Yes, TERA is still good but i'm not fully enjoying myself with this new leveling system. The worlds that you skip over (for anyone new and didn't know about this) still exist, entirely, and they're very fun. The quests are still there too! They're just not in your tracker, and it's so sad. I know this may sound too 'sentimental' for an MMO game but these worlds are beautiful, people put their time and hard work into creating these worlds and quests to have them all looked over? No. You're not getting that from me. I'm questing how the game was intended to quest me.
Please, don't coddle the players. Whoever is whining because they aren't a level whatever yet after all these quests should go find another MMO to play, because i enjoyed TERA as it was before--GRINDING..

Nope. If you are specifically trying to play the AC games in order so as to follow Desmond's plot, then by all means play this game; but when considered in terms of whether this game is actually worth your time as a game, independent of its significance to a plotline you're following? Don't bother.
The game has pretty graphics, and animals and hunting, and all sorts of things that are all well and good, but ultimately feels like a rather lazy attempt at an AC game. For ease of reading, here's a list of my complaints thus far*:
-Control of your character has been paired down to 2 buttons, leaving most situations feeling either too simple or too constraining.
-Combat controls are less fluid than previous games (in part as a consequence of only using 2 buttons)
-Much of the wholly new content feels gimmicky or half-complete, with the exception of the naval stuff. The naval stuff still suffers from some of the other problems, but it's definitely fun and new content.
-Totally phoned-in voice acting
-Terribly written; glaring plot holes, and confusing or poorly justified character motives
-bizarrely obvious tropes; like playing through a mixtape of overused scenes from super-generic movies.
-1 dimensional protagonist (looking at other reviews, this persists throughout the game)
-Main character assumes an Irish name rooted in a celtic word so that he may more easily pass as an Italian or Spaniard... seriously, this is the reason given. -_-;
*I currently have 16.8 hrs on record. Despite my 'no' review, I do intend to finish this game. If at any point I feel this review needs revision, or my opinion of the game has changed I will do so immediately, but unfortunately I suspect this will wind up being my final verdict.

The most fun thing you do is (Hence the title of the F*cking game) assassinate people, and you only do that half the time. Truely an amazing game. Jump scares are known to be cheap thrills and they get a lot of slack for that, but I actually think that is very unfair to generalize so broadly. Jump scares are considered cheap because so many games/movies/whatever do them sooooo poorly. But this game, and the whole series, delivers them incredibly effectively.
I think 3 was a good idea in changing the formula, but I am very happy with how this came back to the formula that worked so well but made audio so much more important. Giving patience to listen while you are stressed about so many other factors really adds to the tension. You really decide your fate by paying enough attention and when all that tension comes to a mistake it is your fault and the jump-scare is that much more effective.
I do agree with many in saying that the animatronics are too gruesome and it is taking away from the effect it had before. In the original, the soulless eyes but otherwise unthreatening demeanor was what made them so effective to me.
Keep up the outstanding effort.

Pros
+Gameplay is definitely fast paced and theres a lot of variety in weaponry
+Graphically game looks fairly above average
+The soundtrack is fairly fitting
Cons
-Feels more like a game in alpha then in beta, not really something for early access (imo)
-Controls can be a little clunky at times
-A few bugs with the text showing up with numbers and korean text
-Very few choices in maps and even fewer in game modes
Overall
I can't really recommend this game right now just because it feels too early especially for the prices. I feel like it has a lot of potential and it can be really great and fun once it gets a few updates with content updates and fixes and such. I'd feel better if the price was lowered for the time being (call me cheap if you want but for what the game has it feels closer to a 10-15$ game tops). I personally refunded it a little after posting this review since I can't see myself going back to it for the time being. I'll probably pick it up down the road if it ends up getting much more improvements. I've read on the forums they plan to add coop pve which sounds pretty fun.
tl;dr
Feels more like an alpha then something that should be in EA. A bit too pricey for what the game actually has. Theres potential down the road for something good but can't recommend at the moment.

This game is going to get a great competitive scene going I think.

list of other free benchmark programs
passmark/performance test : will test your CPU, GPU, RAM, & DISK DRIVES as well as lets you compare your performance scores to the avg scores for your components and other components. free full 30 day trial 29.99 after trial at
(warning AMD users, this program does favor Nvidia gpu's and AMD scores no where near what Nvidia does on this program but great for benching other components)
3dmark ,vantage, 11,  : the free demo versions availible can be used forever and bench you GPU and CPU as well as lets you compare to others. prices for full unlocked versions. 3d mark vantage 9.99, 3d mark 11 14.99, and 3d mark 19.99 all on steam.
unigen heaven benchmark : completely free and a beautiful benchmark but only benches GPU performance
unigen vally : another completely free bench tool and very beautiful GPU performence bench
there is more out there, but these are some i personally use and trust.

Gameplay is mostly the same, barring new features and the fact that (for some reason) dino capturing takes two button presses. The graphics are good, though it took a little doing to figure everything out.
My big gripe with this updated game is the sound. A lot of the sound effects chosen simply DO NOT FIT. I know it's hard to think about immersion with a 2D single-screen platformer, but some of the sounds kicked me out, and hard. Those audio footprints HURT, dammit.

Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six: Siege is a pure tactical game that brings you intense actions. It's highly focused on teamwork, tactical decisions, strategies, and many more. It never fails me to bring some intense moments and situations especially in a firefight.
Quick History
At launch, it had a rough start but soon after, the community and the player base quickly rises. The new content, updates, bug fixes just caused the game to have the biggest comeback in gaming history. The game just keeps rolling.
Gameplay
The gunplay is top solid. It is. You can strafe/lean to give you more of a tactical vibe. The spread on hip firing is indeed insane so most of the time you have to aim down sights. The recoil is high (not insanely high) which is good since it requires skills to secure a kill. But never be greedy for kills because if you are, things will get badly).
The mechanics in this game is astonishing-the interactions and the animations of using your gadgets and items. I won't forget about the stunning destructive environment that you can cause to make it as an advantage for both defenders and attackers.
Operators
In this game, there are operators. Each operators are very unique and has their own gadgets that can turn the tide of any battle. Choose the ones that suits your play-style. And yes, there were some operators that received some nerfs and buffs but it's still balanced.
Game Modes
There are three game modes in this game: Defusing the Bomb, Hostage, and Securing the Area.
Defusing the Bomb: The defenders have to defend two bomb sites, while the attackers have to go in, plant the defuser, and defend the defuser from the defenders.
Hostage: Defenders have to keep the hostage secure while the attackers attempts to rescue the hostage.
Securing the Area: Defenders have to secure the biohazard container while the attackers go in, get in range of the area, and secure it.
Community
Well...the community. People have said that the community is toxic. There were team killers, toxic people, and trollers. All of that sums up to toxic people. Not all people in the community are toxic though. In my perspective and experience, there are some friendly people that just plays the game and chill. But I've only run into some toxic people a few times (note that these are from my experience).

Summary
Overall, I believe it's one of the most tactical shooters out there, the game is quite balanced, and it's a very solid game. I have not suffer major fps drops (run on very high). Surprisingly, I haven't run into any hackers so far. The hit registration is meh, the servers are meh (please make the servers better), some bugs here and there,but doesn't bother me sometimes.

I recommend this game, but it does have its problems.
It is an interesting new take on the Five Nights At Freddy's formula. You still have to survive a night and if you don't you will be killed by animatronics, but the twist is that it's a pizzeria tycoon game! This is cool especially since the night can theoretically go on forever until you complete all of your tasks for the night. This is a very interesting way to shake up the FNAF formula.
What I have a problem with, however, is that sometimes it seems like this game is too hard. I don't know what it is, but sometimes I feel like the animatronics, no matter how far away from the room they are, can just rush towards your vent whenever they feel like it. For example, just before I was playing on the 4th Night. I was doing good, my tasks were getting done and I was meticulously checking my motion detector and audio. Springtrap was at the exact other side of the restaurant. I put down an audio to keep him there, went to do one of my tasks, then Springtrap IMMEDIATELY killed me.
The one thing I disliked about FNAF 3 is that the balloon boy sound was very unreliable and didn't always work on Springtrap. It seems I'm having the same problem but tenfold now.

UPDATE!: Even though its only a few days since launch they have already polished the gameplay by A LOT so there is no longer animation tearing and the game feels alot more responsive. They have also fixed the translation bug and almost everything is Translated. Forge / Storage doesnt appear to have been added yet.
So i did a 3 hour first look stream of the game which is now on my youtube ZoulsGaming which you can check out if you want some pure unedited gameplay. This is a case where i wish there was a "meh" button. The main quirk people has is the UI not being fully translated. Luckily they have said that they are working on that to get it fixed as soon as possible.
There is everything they promised. mutliple armor sets with different values, character creation including gender. a variety of weapons all with different attacks and strengths / weaknesses. both PVP and PVE gameplay. BUT. The animation and hit detection is really really bad right now due to it being early access and the combat feels really clunky. As soon as they fix that (which i know is no minor task) there is more than enough content in the game.
So buy the game if you wants to support the game and likes hack'n'slash combat, but while this is one of the more fleshed out early access its STILL early access and there are some things which needs to be fixed.
My best bid would be come back 1 or 2 weeks after this review is posted and see how it works then.
It needs some polishing for now but combat was fun enough and devs were responsive. I think it will become better and better

Here's the thing. I like action games like that. I like melee arenas and there was a gap in me that needed to be filled... but at this stage Versus just can't fill it yet. It's way too frustrating.
I ain't gonna spend time to talk about GFX or Sound so I will go straight into the gameplay, where most of my issues are.
Combat feel really clunky. One time I'm magically teleported ( i presume lag ?) other times I'm stunned for no reason or just grabbed even though I was far away from the enemy LOL. The worst part is when you get hit with a Giant Sword. When you are downed they can kill you in one blow even though your HP is more than half. I haven't figured out the move for it yet.
*EDIT*
The game has been patched couple of times and it's even worse than it was before. Adding more health doesn't solve anything. It makes overpowered players even more powerful. First off I had problems finding a match today. There was ONLY 1 player. Xenox. Not only One Handed sword can stun lock you but also he had good armor and weapon on him. So I had to attack him many more times before he died while he could execute 2-3 hit combo which stun locked me ( even though I was pressing evade and sometimes Counter, nothing seemed to work, while being stun locked that is ) and then I died since I don't have good items to go on par with him. Where is the proper matchmaking for this game? On top of it MANY attacks seem to have a weird hitboxes. My katana counter missed so many times even though clearly enemy was in front of me?! WTF. The same goes for Giant Axe counter it just missed so whats the point?! It is really frustrating when the game is so flawed and unbalanced. I recommend waiting before buying it. Honestly.
Decrease the health as it was better and faster now it's harder to kill players with better gear.
Some attacks don't make any sense to me as Block Breaker can be parried ( which One Handed players love to wait until you attack and then combo/stun lock you to death ). Giant Swords Charged Attack, I tried to parry it but it seems like there are some specific frames you have to aim for... no success so far.
There is also a glitch that lets you Grab a player constantly even when downed... Add insult to injury some attacks can hit downed enemies but if you have sword and shield you cant do that lol Unbalance continues....
Community is shi*. When I played 2v2 I wanted to go 1v1 but it was impossible. Everyone just runs like mad button mash and tries to get the stun first. No chivarly like in Dark Souls lol...
*EDIT* Because of low player base its easier now to play 1v1 and people seem to prefer that which is good for practising skills.
I died so many time for BS reasons or by groups and hitboxes or hit detection when fighting groups is just RANDOM. One time when I had giant sword I thought I would hit 2-3 enemies at a time because they were grouped BUT INSTEAD I got interrupted by their attack ( even tho I had full armor ) and killed. It seems like some attacks have super armor and weird hitboxes. Other time I was 2v1 a guy with a long sword and he somehow manged to stunlock BOTH of us and killed me... What the heck. Until those issues are resolved and the gameplay and animations feel fluid/smooth I can't recommend this game.

This software tests the Mantle technology that some modern Graphic Cards are able to use. Mantle is supposed to boost the performance of a game/3D engine by giving it a deeper control over the graphic board.
I was skeptical about this new technology. That was until I ran this test.
Average FPS with DirectX 11:   20.36
Average FPS with Mantle:        38.66   (89,88% more under the same conditions!)
Just to be emphatic, any comparison will only be relevant when running on a MANTLE COMPATIBLE HARDWARE, and under the same conditions. If you don't have it, don't worry; you're just missing a hardware test. If you're really curious you can simply see how it is on YouTube.
Great hardware stress test. Allows custom settings too!
EDIT: Mantle must no longer be used. That's what their own website say. They are moving on to something better and more widely accepted (Nvidia and Intel didn't like when their rival, AMD, created it).
Mantle may not have been a commercial success, but made everyone rush to catch up with the "low level API" idea. Without Mantle we wouldn't have the new tools in DirectX 12 and the Next-Generation OpenGL.
Still, a curious stress test if you have a GPU supporting Mantle.

I genuinely dont understand these comments about the launcher having issues or the game not having certain graphical features. The game looks absolutely incredible. I've ran into no issues at all in the game, no glitches, no exploits, graphical issues, or any of that preposterousness. I have only played the Video game version, I never even heard of Talisman as a kid probably because we were all into Dungeons and Dragons original paper and dice game. I have played extensively on This Digital Deluxe version of Talisman now and can render the following Analysis:
Keeping in mind that it IS still in Pre-release stage overall it is an enjoyable gaming experience one can play with the whole family (Up to 4 players).
Pros:
1.) Simple to learn and play
2.) Ease of use - the game is entirely mouse driven. One can play with the keyboard sitting on the desk, feet kicked up ... using only the mouse as you relax in your favorite chair.
3.) In-game voice chat which can be muted by individual player
4.) Fantasy based ... always a plus :)
5.) Family Friendly - as long as you are not overly religious (Devils, demons, angels, undead etc are contained within)
6.) A Mandatory Random setting!!! The host can set the game to Classic mode where no perks (Runes) can be used and all class choices are random, this is an option missing from other games (DoTP needs this badly)

Cons:
1.) Glitches up terribly in Multi-player if someone leaves the game normally locking it up. (SP w/Bots works fine)
2.) Game glitches if you alt/tab out to do something else
3.) Re-playability isn't that good. It takes a couple of games to see all the spells and Adventure cards but once you have run through them once or twice, things tend to get repetative. They definitely need a wider range of spells and adventure cards.
4.) Class balance isn't that good. Some classes are very noticeably more powerful than other classes and have abilities that give much greater advantages over other players (Prophetess and assassin come to mind)
5.) Using AI's in Multi-player runs the risk of hanging the game up. Bots usually get hung up in the City at the alchemist and they go into an infinite loop and the game cannot progress from there but as of 1-7-2014 using all humans in MP games hasn't botched up unless someone rages quits .... which is common if the game is not going their way.
Overall I would recommend this game as I expect all these problems to be worked out before its final release version.

The protagonist wakes in a strange home with no recollection of what brought him there - but a few encounters with dead bodies, bloodstains, and abandoned weapons make it clear that the circumstances are grim. You move this highly pixelated character through highly pixelated 2D environments, interacting with doors, ladders, and objects as you try to piece together a growing mystery.
The game is a very short, very inexpensive experiment that is intriguing in the way it builds tension only to leave you with more questions than answers. You might return to it multiple times hoping to fill in the gaps, but ultimately realize that the game wasn't really telling you a complete story.
is as much a choose your own adventure novel as a game, but the story it tells is disturbing and unique enough to hold interest despite limited interactivity. Pick up a knife, or leave it be. Watch a videotape, or let well enough alone. It's not always clear what impact these decisions might have at the time, and in fact, it may not be any clearer what the impact was once you finish.
may not feature enough actual game for some players, but
has successfully made a sophisticated, horrifying story.

| GREAT | AMAZING | MASTERPIECE

This is an interesting game. I'd describe it as a sort of point and click adventure game, with the story being about a murder mystery. It's not very long, but I think it's still pretty good, since there's some variety in playthroughs; depending on how much you explore or how many objects you interact with, the story might be a bit different. Not a lot different, but you might end up with different conclusions depending on what you did (or didn't do).
The art style is a very simple pixel graphics one. There's plenty of games of varying quality using such a style, which most of the time just do it for the nostalgia factor; I'd say that in the case of Home, it worked, especially given the gameplay. As for the sound, it also keeps the tone of an old-school game.
The game page describes the game as being a horror adventure, but as I said in the opening paragraph, it's more of a murder mystery. There's still several parts that can be quite unsettling, and again, depending on how much you explore, you might fid even more questions. And that's another thing; by the end of the game, you'll probably have more questions than answers; even the things that sort of get answered leave a lot of doubts. While some people might dislike that kind of open ended stories, I found it somewhat enjoyable.
Well, in conclusion, Home is a short, enjoyable game, so I recommend it.

Home is simple in concept, but very well executed. It's more or less a point and click game (well, more like spacebar and down arrow key, but whatever) that really brings you back to the days of text based books and stories. Although it's definitely a visual adventure, it really gave me nostalgia for all of the (don't laugh) Neopets users' text-based adventures from long ago.
Home isn't particularly scary, but the story definitely gets you hooked. I found myself relaxed and ready for more by the time I completed my first play though, and was interested to know more about the world. The world itself is all pixel art - and although not the best art I have seen, the artist ulitized his capabilities well and really took time to design a very atmospheric setting. The sounds in the game were well placed, and generally high quality.
I personally picked this up in a Humble Bundle, but I'd say it's worth a full price buy if you're looking to spend a few hours (if you do multiple playthroughs - one playthrough takes roughly an hour) solving a mystery.

I am the first to review this game?  Wow.
Stumbled into this game while I was looking for something else entirely.  Ended up abandoning the search for that something else the instant this caught my eye as I definitely could not resist acquiring this.
Those who grew up in the early 80's will probably remember playing the original game here.  I've played this very, very often and these days I have to use a Commodore Emulator to do so.  The original was a challenge and continues to be such even today.
Acquiring the achievements for the Emerald Dinosaurs has been pretty easy.  One thing I definitely noticed with the Emerald Parasaur is that it has the added difficulty of being able to break out of its cage after 10 - 20 seconds.  That was a nice surprise and it even comes with a sound effect that is opposite of the one used when the cage is created.
Want to let all your eggs hatch all in one go?  No problem!  You can do just that if you desired it...as long as you're not doing the Classic Game Mode.  You will want to make sure to be very patient and avoid Dino Mom during all of this, too.  You can even hatch eggs on the same platform level as others.  I have had somewhere around 10 dinos on one platform in cages.  Just beware you don't accidentally run into one that is not caged as sometimes it will be very difficult to see them amongst the pack even though the uncaptured ones stand out in that they are not darkened.
Other than the added difficulty as well as the extended storyline that is incorporated into even the multiple tutorial levels the game plays true to the original.  Instead of a percentage guage counting down toward Devolution you get a meter appearing right beside you when you are hit.  Only the final 10% of the countdown will show any numbers, which should make that one achievement regarding that quite easy to obtain.

If I could sum up my experience with Wings of Vi, I'd have to say that - in stark contrast to the advertising - it's an arbitrarily difficult game (Keep in mind this statement is coming from someone who has played through most of I Wanna Be the Guy). Though I have to admit the art style and environments are impressive, the gameplay itself is mediocre at best; you play as an angel Vi who, after letting loose an ancient demon, has to run around trying to stop him along with her friend Ruby (who usually makes the situation more complicated). This involves running around and making sure you don't fall into different traps, killing enemies with quite possibly the weakest offense in the game (at least starting off), and gaining different power ups along the way that enhance your platforming skills. However, before I continue, I want to address what specifically was good and bad:
Good - As mentioned above, the aesthetics are great, and they're probably the only reason why I managed to play for so long. Along this, the character customization seems somewhat in depth, and what little I do know about the plot didn't turn me off from the experience.
Bad - The game is most certainly arbitrarily difficult, and the game spikes in difficulty for no reason in certain places. Alongside this, the hit box can be incredibly fat at VERY crucial points. While the game does teach you certain basic elements of gameplay through showing instead of telling, this style of teaching is quickly tossed out the window in favor of the style of I Wanna Be the Guy - constant death, very little progress, and no hints as far as how to get through. Ultimately, the game fails to show you that you can indeed beat the game and have fun; by doing this, it loses all sense of reward.
If you're dead set on playing this game, just wait until the price drops. Either that, or go on YouTube and watch someone else's playthrough of the game.

Now the upside here is the Mantle support for AMD users. It helped me get a better feel for my system/GPU and where I stand. I compare this to 3DMark 11 and it falls short. 3DMark shows much more extensive information and provides in which to compare to other users. The website shows a ranking for each users test and allows you to see what components they have that might have made a difference.
Example, I ran 3DMark and found I was 8216 ranked. Another person was similar, and the number one with my same CPU and GPU had 12,000 points. I was able to look into their build and see that they were running a second graphics card and had overclocked it for the test. That was nice to know and physically see what a second card might do for me.
3DMark as well as this, is also free. You'll need to pay in 3DMark to unlock additional features, resolutions, etc that you don't have to do here. That's the downside to that software.
All in all, this is a worthwhile test that really does put the stress on your system. I'm satisfied with the results and could definitely see where my system struggled through the large scale battles (with explosions, laser fire, and more all going on at the same time). As I said, the biggest plus about it, this was just fun to watch (unlike 3DMark which I actually fell asleep to).
I only wish that this was more popular then it is, mainly to have a general idea of what others are pushing with their rigs.

Having bought this within the first minute it was released, I was eager to see what it had to bring to the table of combat. You'll notice upon opening the game, the likes of errors and some messages come up in Korean rather than English. To which I just wave them by and continue with the game. It starts with making a character (of which there are 5 slots) and with each character you can choose whether you want them to be male/female, as well as check out different armour styles (if any), actions and combat styles. It goes on to customize the characters body type, skin colour, facial structure and just the general customisation you find in games. To be honest, I didn't expect this game to have any customisation whatsoever, so I was happy from the start.
Moving on, it takes you through a basic tutorial where you learn to pick items up, hack/slash, use a powerful attack and block. It then goes on to test you in a real arena! A colosseum! First against a team of 2 amateurs, followed by a knight in shining gold armour. Do it for yourself to find out what happens next ;).
Anyhow, it has an armoury, skill page, records/leaderboards page and an inaccessable market (for now I assume since it's early days). I didn't find the game to crash, lag or have any frame drops. However when recording a first look/review video for it, as it changed from the home screen to full screen it did irreversibly crash. However without recording material, the game was flawless.
The gameplay was great, but rather than the average; smash LMB to win. It has dashing, positional blocking, counters, taunts, power moves and as mentioned the 7 different combat styles using different weapons. Deathmatch, Team deathmatch across 3 maps for now and the community of like 30 people who have been on in this first hour have been friendly :P.
Upon victory/defeat, you can get particular items (I got some better boots for my armour), experience and gold etc.
Animations are good, graphics are good, sound is good;
To summarize, it's a typical Korean hack/slash MMO, which actually requires skill and I'm looking forward to playing it much more from now. If you have an opportunity to get it, don't just read reviews but check out this youtube video below, as it will show you everything: from the main menu character customisation, all the way through the armoury, skill sets, combat styles, in game tutorial and online play and finally to the end screen to receive rewards (All under 10 minutes :P ).

TL;DR: Designed for children of the modern era, not for fans of the original games.
Difficulty: Easy - The game poses little challenge to anyone but children of the modern era, with one one or two small moments where some thought or skill is required.
Graphics: Good - Consistent style persists throughout and while I don't personally like the childish theme or the re-design of the main character, there's nothing too bad about the graphical direction in general.
Mechanics: Decent - Most mechanics are used enough in general play to warrant being there and most of varying amount of attacks are satisfying to use. Although there is one attack that I never used because there was never had a moment where it could have been useful.
Conveyance: Decent - A little over the top with the controls, but generally nothing offensive; The game's forward path was always obvious.
Music: Good direction, the mood of the scene was conveyed well enough, but the music was nothing memorable; I don't think there was much reference to the old games' music but if there was then it didn't trigger any kind of nostalgia.
Bug: When I got to the part of the game where you jump from airship to airship, the second airship did not show up for me until after I killed myself.

Considerign Rocket Knight for the megadrive/genesis is my favourtie game of all time, this game has been on my radar for a while. And now, it's finally on sale, and I can play it. And... I'm not exactly impressed.
Lets start off with the issues gameplay wise. The controls are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. I dunno how to fully describe them, they just seem... Scattered. On the original genesis (something I'll compare this game to a lot) the contols were simple. Jump. Swing sword/fire projectile.
Easy.
Now on this, you have Jump, Zoom, Range attack and Melee attack. And they're scattered over the keyboard like no-ones business, Left control, shift, Enter? My god, I'll get hand cramps in a femtosecond! So pick up a controller. The game isn't built for a controller, but it works. Tutorials still say stuff like 'Press control to do this' so there is some experimenting, but for the most part it works ok.
Next, the range attack. It wasn't implemented in the original as it is now, in the original, you would launch a range attack WITH the melee, now they're binded differently. This isn't a problem, the problem comes with the fact that it isn't all that long range, and IT DOESN'T ONE SHOT. That small factor is awful, especially considering the 'zoom attack' does one shot, and has the same amount of range. Not Ideal.
So then, we move to issues with stuff that won't directly effect the gameplay. Sparkster seems somewhat Childish, something I didn't expect, considering he's a KNIGHT and he saves a princess and all that. His rival (which I only just found out was called Axel) is a little♥♥♥♥♥♥ who acts like a baby when you beat him, and doesn't seem to have a noble reason to hate sparkster, unlike in the first game, where he had an evil sort of grin, and acted just right to be his rival.
Music: Haven't hear much, it sounds really good actually. Good remix of the song from the first game.
So, in conclusion: This game compared to the original is atrocious. If you've played the original, you won't like this. But, if you haven't played it, this game might be worth picking up in a steam sale.

I can't help but enjoy the mad cap chaos of this game. With the procedural generation of the levels, so many varied character classes to chose from, and so many different items to find and use together, it offers massive replayability.
I played a game just now, I was playing as a trigger happy soldier, and found a 'bracelet of strength' ... Yeah, this game mixes genres a fair bit, it brings together but not limited to, cannibals, killer robots and vampires ... and spent the next 15 minutes smashing my way through the missions on offer. There's something so satifying about whacking a goon with a baseball bat through a wall and into the bar next door before he has a chance to pull his gun on you!
Another fun character class to play is the hacker; it requires you to think a little more strategically because you're not a strong class, but you have infinite 'hacks' you can use on electronics. These include the standard computer consoles scattered about in various complexs, allowing you to redirect and vent poison to clear out their inhabitants, open prison doors to cause chaos, and so on. You can also hack TV sets and cause them to explode (great for a stealth kill to avoid the cops), and one of my favourites, you can also hack refridgerators and make them 'run'. You have to play it to see, but you can cause some great chain reactions. And that's the key as to why this game is so much fun, one little decision can spawn chaos and turn the tide of a game.

Very fun, very addictive, very cute (at the same time ferocious). The gameplay is a bit hard in the beginning and the bosses seems almost impossible but it gets a bit easier after 1-2 hours of playing.  Only problem is that the starting can kill you instantly if you're not ready so don't think you can just jump in and wing it.  A lot of the time you will encounter mobs that are way to high level for you to handle (especially bosses that are easily triggered) and the moment this happens you're pretty much screwed if you haven't found the level exit.  Love the gathering, crafting and storing mechanics.  Gathering resources are quite fun and simple, all you do is aim, collect and pray you don't summon a boss.  Crafting is pretty much combining random resources together to create weapons, armours, etc.  I think it is pretty cool, however, making the recipes to be tier based, meaning you can only combine ingredients of the same tier to create weapons and armours of that tier.  This prevent players from randomly crafting an OP sword at the start.  The game also allows you to store items as back up for when die, and you definately will.  The storage is also accessible by your other avatars, even those from different factions, so if you create a mage weapon by accident you just store for your mage avatar.  Controls are very smooth and gives alot of freedom, espescially with the jump mechanics.  The pixelated graphics are amazing.  Rarely lags on high settings.  And the best part is multiplayer is pretty simple to set-up.  Just select "New Server" and send your mates the IP shown. No need for hamachi.

Little did I know that it was basically "craft the narrative yourself". Imagine the following:
"You opened the box. Inside there was..."
"1. A banana"
"2. Nothing"
"3. A box of crayons"
Then, nothing about the gameplay changes. It just changes a few texts in the rest of the otherwise identical game.
The game is a "mystery" about what happaned to your family, but you are just tasked with picking the choice. Again, it's not "take a guess" and that you might be wrong. It's about you choosing, literally *choosing* what happened through a menu system when prompted. No mystery at all.
Simply put: Dear Esther is a more artistic experience. To the Moon is a better story experience. Home is mediocre in both.

An empty psychological "horror" with no intellectual or scare payoff.
The game play becomes sluggish and repetitive because every interaction works so slow (each door, ladder, bush, etc, requires its own individual cutscene). The narrative thinks highly of itself, despite having no complexity. The story doesn't challenge your perception of events in any meaningful way. The writing is a cop out, as it is constantly asking the player, "Did this happen?", "Did I do that?", "Why/What/Where/Who/When?" instead of having the player organically question events themselves. Show, don't tell.
What I can complement Home on is that it conveys a spooky atmosphere, and leaves you anticipating something scary (though "something scary" never comes). What this game ultimately is though, is a spooky, find-the-narrative-bread-crumbs video game, fit for pre-teens who are faint of heart.

/h1 Wonderful
Note: Not a full review since I haven't finished but I've played 90 hours so far.
Also Note: I'm not good at writing reviews.
/b Opinion of the Upsides
I highly recommend playing this game if you love the AC series, are new to it, or have been disappointed for the last few years of AC games. This is the game that redeems itself from the previous titles. It is not perfect but it is much better. For the 90 hours I've played so far, I reached lvl 40. Exploring has been really fun and a lot of locations to see. Locations are beautiful anywhere you go and I recommend taking some pictures. Like everyone else says, this is much better than the recent previous Assassin's Creed games that have came out. So far, the story has more depth to it and the main character's purpose to do what he does makes more sense and has more emotion for the player to feel. As for the combat, I'd say it imporved a lot.
/b Weapons & Combat
The different weapon types are fun to use. Some weapons have downsides compared to it's upsides. Like in any RPG game, heavy weapons obviously make you more vulnerable because they're slower but do huge amounts of damage. Light weapons are quick but have less damage so you can move super fast to avoid arrows and such. There are long range weapons which do medium amount of damage but have longer reach, obviously. The bow is questionable on how you would use it in real life but they provide a simple variety that are self explanatory like the shotgun bow, quick bow, sniper bow, and the balanced one. There are firebombs which provide good distractions or if you just want to burn something. There isn't much use of it later once you have other weapons that use fire. Sleep darts are extremely useful if you don't want to leave random dead bodies everywhere and you can escape combat by using this on the people chasing you. Berserk darts can turn your enemies against each other but I don't use it much. Poison darts can do small amounts of damage over time and can spread over some other enemies.
You will get a lot of weapons over time and I recommend selling the ones you don't need if and use that money to upgrade the ones you like. Another way is that you can scrap the parts and upgrade your gear for materials. Once you have fully upgraded your gear then you should just sell your unwanted weapons. I recommend not upgrading as often unless your weapons are below about 3-6 levels. Once you upgraded all your gear, hunting and looking for materials would become pretty much useless unless you need to sell them for money or need them for a quest.
Navigating Egypt's oceans and rivers is quite pretty. However, other than enemies patroling and some npc's sailing, there isn't much to do there. There are Trireme's carrying supplies with some guards. There are some shipwrecks to explore.
/b Downsides
There are some downsides to this game, like in every game. Looking around in the oceans and rivers is quite boring since there's nothing to do unless there's a shipwreck or sunken ruins. Senu, Bayek's hawk, can pretty much find any lootable chests, locations, animals and enemies. Animus pulse helps you find missing pots, inestigation areas, and chests. I feel that those two features give away the fun for some people that just want to get into somewhere and find things for themselves. However, you can't help but use it because it's almost necessary to use.
Combat is pretty fun and quite different from previous Assassin's Creed Titles. Sometimes it can be buggy because of different surfaces. The lockon system is fustrating to use so I just fight without locking on. It's weird how enemies have unilimted arrows and spears to just throw at you.
Hard mode is pretty easy. Since the beginning of the game, I explored everything there is to explore and do as a quest in the reigons where the main story is currently taking you and you get up levels above the main story's level and combat is easier because of this. Most of the time there is no challenge because of the level difference. The only challenge would be fighting boss fights or if you would get overwhelmed by enemies.
Sneaking is rewarding but I feel that in some areas, enemies should be able to see you in bushes like when you're moving in them or when it's really bright outside.
Ubisoft does a lot of hand holding with players. Exploring egypt can be a fun and crazy adventure. But Ubisoft makes it easier for players. Like I said before, if you were to explore the ocean or deep rivers, you wouldn't find anything rewarding or good looking, just empty ocean unless it's a marked place on your map. Senu replaces eagle vision but Senu still automatically marks enemies on the map so you could see them in real time. Because Senu marks exactly where certain loot chests are, it takes away the fun of trying to look for it yourself. Marking enemies on the map obscures some of your vision if you are trying to look at the details of their character but that isn't much of a problem. The sniper bow has a special ability in which if you hold the shoot button then you can control the arrow. I feel that this is too much of a feature even though it is  very fun to use.
/b I Hope...
In future Assassin's Creed games, I hope that there will be no minimaps or much hud at all to keep the game immersive. I hope thatif future titles will follow this rpg style then they would improve by providing more unique varieties in weapons, abilities, gear espeically, and other customization options. I hope, that if the next games have naval combat then they would expand on it more than what they did in Black Flag, if at all possible. I hope that there will be more story outside the animus. I hope that story telling will keep being good rather than having dull characters and a dull plot. I hope future AC games like this will keep having as much content as this one and I hope Ubisoft will expand on this RPG genre to make  more content rich games that are not boring.

I've ran into no issues at all in the game, no glitches, no exploits, graphical issues, or any of that preposterousness.
